## DL-165  MS8 8a: frozen-criteria loader, ramp-run config S5_ramp.yaml, runner gate    [ID: MS8, D35, H-2, H-3, DL-084, DL-157, DL-164]
Date:            2026-10-17        Author:
Decision:        First MS8 code change, as DL-164 ordered. New src/mprsurge/criteria.py (verify_frozen_criteria, load_frozen_criteria, require_frozen_for_config). It refuses to run (CriteriaError, a ConfigError, so the runner exits 2 with "config error") on: (1) tag criteria-frozen missing or lightweight (no message); (2) no SHA-256 in the tag message in the DL-164 format; (3) the tag blob (git show criteria-frozen:configs/robustness_criteria.yaml, CRLF normalised to LF) hashing to something else than the tag message; (4) the working file hashing (LF text) to something else than the tag message, for the criteria file and for the three secondary files named in the tag message (S13.yaml, A4_grids.yaml, S5_cells.yaml); (5) any of the four listed as modified or untracked by git status. load_frozen_criteria parses the verified blob of the tag, not the working file. Reading only; no frozen file is touched. Wiring (sheet row H-2): runner build_plan calls require_frozen_for_config, which acts only on a config whose robustness.criteria_file is configs/robustness_criteria.yaml; new configs/S5_ramp.yaml (headline cell, self-contained, names the frozen file; robustness.* is outside the hash view, so its config hash equals configs/S5.yaml's); A4, A0, A1, A2 stay on configs/replication.yaml; S5.yaml, the timing cells and S13.yaml are unchanged, so no stored hash moves. provenance.make_run_record hashes the frozen file as LF text (criteria_sha256 = c7d2f36b...), other criteria files still as bytes (replication.py compares those). ## DL-169  MS8 8b: owner rulings M-1 to M-12 and M-9 key confirmation, as applied; one departure from M-10's wording (coupling base step 5e-5 tau)    [ID: MS8, D43, S5, S13, F-14, F-19, M-1 to M-12, DL-166, DL-168]
Date:            2026-10-17        Author:
Decision:        Rulings of the reviewer, agreed by the project owner (8b prompt), recorded as given. M-1: P2 noise seeds at all 13 T_ramp, linear, 10 seeds (130 runs). M-2: start-distance runs {0.5, 1.5, 3} on P1 at the 13 T_ramp, linear only, the 1.5 run reused (26 new runs). M-3: NOT adopted; no extra headline start-distance runs; headline RB5 = the delta0 ladder (S13) plus the P1 start-distance runs (S5); the owner may add 2 runs later. M-4: floor = 3 D43 levels x 4 Heun rungs x 10 seeds at delta0 1e-6 (D26 default), 120 runs. M-5: one Radau run, 120 s, rtol 1e-10 (DL-100 (3)). M-6: the S5 part is judged against the whole shared Table 9.1 row (S2, S5, S6). M-7: a null start distance stays out of the config hash view, so no stored hash changes. M-8: a seed-key prefix in the runner, so no sweep cell uses the bare key [seed]. M-9: seed keys [8, 1, s] (s = 0..9, S5 P2 noise) and [8, 2, l, s] (l = 0..2, floor and Heun ladder; the four rungs of one (l, s) share the key) are confirmed; they are no longer UNVERIFIED proposals. M-10: coupled Heun increments as the F-14 entry (DL-152) states. M-11: storage layout as recommended in docs/ms8_plan.md (8 float64 arrays at 1 kHz, kept). M-12: longest-first job order as recommended there.
  Departure from the wording of M-10 in docs/ms8_plan.md, found while implementing, reported for the owner: the M-10 option says "draw the dt 1e-4 increments and sum 10, 5 and 2 of them for the coarser rungs". That gives rungs of 1e-3, 5e-4 and 2e-4; the F-14 ladder is {1e-3, 5e-4, 2.5e-4, 1e-4}, and 2.5e-4 is 2.5 draws of 1e-4. F-14 itself (each finer rung's increments sum to the 1e-3 rung's, per seed) is kept exactly. Implementation: the increments are drawn at the largest step that divides all four rungs, 5e-5 tau, and each rung sums 20, 10, 5 and 2 of them (noise.coupling_dt_tau = 5e-5); every rung's increments then sum to the 1e-3 rung's, and the finer rungs are also nested in each other. The 5e-5 value is derived from the ladder, not taken from a source: UNVERIFIED, for the owner's ruling before 8e. The alternative (a Brownian bridge refinement of the 1e-3 path) was not built. Consequence: the 1e-3 rung of a floor run has not the stream of a plain mode-N run (as M-10 already said), and every rung draws tau/5e-5 = 3.34e8 normals (launch arithmetic, DL-172).
Reason:          instruction of the project owner (8b prompt); the departure is a defect in the arithmetic of the M-10 option, not a change of F-14.
Options:         for the departure: (a) base step 5e-5 (chosen, exact F-14); (b) base step 1e-4 with a 2.5e-4 rung built by a Brownian bridge inside a pair of 1e-4 increments (not built); (c) drop the 2.5e-4 rung (changes the ruled ladder, not allowed here).
Chosen:          as above   Default from: owner rulings, F-14
Test:            tests/test_ms8_coupling.py (12) and tests/test_ms8_runlist.py: block sums, nesting of all four rungs, the new kernel equal to the old bit for bit, chunking independence, refusal of a rung that is not a multiple.
Status:          applied in 8b; the 5e-5 step waits for the owner's confirmation. Nothing run.

## DL-188  MS8 8f2: FINDING, RB3(a) misses at the A4 grid step in all 6 testable runs; stored-data diagnosis    [ID: MS8, 8f2, RB3, A7, DL-179, DL-182, DL-186]
Date:            2026-10-18        Author:
Decision:        This is a FINDING (the frozen rule applied as ruled, 0 of 6 within one step), not a departure; no rule changed. src/mprsurge/analysis/rb_diag.py, scripts/run_rb_diag.py (commit 09c9427, git.dirty false), results/A7/rb_diag_ms8.json SHA-256 3fb10f131efe6a40d19459629637aad74a5c2ab95bd9f9651c37835b4af197db (stored data only, no integration). Raw-crossing onset against t_pred, run clock, signed (onset minus t_pred):
  testable (eta not constant at t_pred), P1 linear start distance 0.5 at T_ramp 1, 1.778, 3.162, 5.623, 10 s and P5 linear 1.778 s: eta error -0.829, -0.515, -0.317, -0.189, -0.110 and +0.627; error in A4 steps 33.15, 20.60, 12.68, 7.57, 4.40 and 25.07; time error -0.331, -0.366, -0.401, -0.426, -0.440 and -0.318 s; the A4 step in seconds at the local eta rate at t_pred 0.0100, 0.0178, 0.0316, 0.0562, 0.1000 and 0.0127 s. Constant eta at t_pred (P1 linear 1 s and 1.778 s, P1 sigmoid 1 s, start distance 1.5): time error -0.289, -0.269, -0.266 s, no verdict (ruling 2). In all 9 runs the observed onset is EARLIER than t_pred.
  Growth rate of ln(envelope) over the last decade before the crossing (our definition) against the mean Re lambda at the stored (eta, J) over the same window, ratio: 1.021, 1.017, 1.004, 1.000, 1.004 (start distance 0.5), 0.996, 1.021, 0.994 (constant eta), 1.036 (P5): the local growth rate equals the quasi-static Re lambda within 4 percent. Predicted amplitude at the observed crossing, delta0 exp(I(t_c)) with delta0 1e-6: 3e-5 to 3.2e-4 against the threshold 0.2176 (1e-5 to 3e-5 for the constant-eta runs); ln(threshold / predicted amplitude) 8.86, 8.22, 7.65, 7.04, 6.51 (start distance 0.5, falling with T_ramp), 9.65, 9.01, 8.89 (constant eta), 9.04 (P5); that log gap divided by the observed growth rate gives 0.476, 0.481, 0.496, 0.495, 0.485, 0.291, 0.265, 0.268 and 0.264 s, against the observed leads 0.331, 0.366, 0.401, 0.426, 0.440, 0.289, 0.269, 0.266 and 0.318 s (equal within 1 percent for the three constant-eta runs, where Re lambda is constant). Distance of the stored state from the quasi-static fixed point of M3 at (eta, J, Delta): at t_on |dv| = 1.0e-6 (the kick) and |dr| = 0 in all 9 (by construction); at t_pred |dv| 0.22 to 3.33 and |dr| 0.07 to 0.18 (far outside the linear regime, so t_pred lies after saturation); at the observed crossing |dv| 0.02 to 0.22 and |dr| 0.002 to 0.038. Band-passed envelope at t_on: 2.2e-4 to 2.6e-3 (delta0 is 1e-6).
  Reading [reasoned, not tested]: the numbers do not support a growth-rate mismatch (ratio about 1) and not a state-at-t_on offset (the state is exactly the fixed point plus the kick). They support a start-amplitude offset: the real in-band amplitude was already e^6.5 to e^9.7 (about 700 to 16,000 times) above delta0 exp(I) at the crossing, giving a lead of 0.27 to 0.44 s that varies little with the ramp rate, while one A4 step is 0.01 to 0.1 s at these T_ramp; a one-step match needs |lead| x eta rate below 0.025 (eta rate below about 0.08 per s for a 0.3 s lead), which the in-range runs (T_ramp up to 10 s) do not reach. Whether the offset is the projection of the v-kick onto the unstable mode (the formula uses no eigenvector scaling, A7), a ramp-driven transient in the 25 to 100 Hz band, or the acausal band-pass (sosfiltfilt) smearing the envelope at t_on, is not separated by stored data; the monotone fall of the log gap with T_ramp (8.86 to 6.51) goes with a ramp-driven part, not with a fixed projection factor. Test that would separate it, PROPOSED, not run: P1 start distance 0.5, T_ramp 1 s, delta0 1e-9 and 1e-3 (seconds of run time); a kick-dominated onset shifts by ln(delta0 ratio) / Re lambda, a forced-transient onset does not.

## DL-189  MS8 8f2: FINDING, RB6 solver clause misses (DOP853 against Radau, 181 ms against 1 ms); stored-data diagnosis    [ID: MS8, 8f2, RB6, S13, DL-184, DL-186]
Date:            2026-10-18        Author:
Decision:        FINDING, not a departure; the frozen text is applied literally (ruling 4): class agrees (D-tr, D-tr), onset 58.698 s against 58.879 s (181 ms) with both onsets, bound 1 ms: DOES NOT MEET. Diagnosis from the stored records, results/A7/rb_diag_ms8.json (DL-188), no new simulation. DOP853 rtol 1e-8, 1e-10, 1e-12: onset 58.698 s, delay 0.066192 at all three; Radau rtol 1e-10: onset 58.879 s, delay 0.071471. Storage: t, r, v, s, eta, J, Delta, I are float64 at 1 kHz (np.load dtype float64); v is near -0.5947, so its resolution is about 1.3e-16 (2.2e-16 x 0.5947). Pre-onset envelope (25 to 100 Hz band-pass, Hilbert): after the kick (envelope 2.07e-5 at t_on) it falls to 3.3e-13 at t_on + 0.5 s and then sits on a plateau from about 6 s to about 50 s with median 1.84e-15 and 99th percentile 5.0e-15 (about 14 times the v resolution), with 18 to 28 samples exactly 0.0; the plateau median agrees to 14 digits in all four runs, so it is a floor of float64 storage and the band-pass, not a property of the solver. The analytic prediction delta0 exp(I_min) is 0.0 (I_min = -1122.5, minimum of I at 50.56 s) and t_pred is 115.2 s: the headline onset (58.7 s, 56.5 s before t_pred) is set from the floor, not from the kick. Consistent with this, the delta0 ladder 1e-9, 1e-6, 1e-3 gives the same onset 58.698 s (DL-183). Above the plateau the growth rate of ln(envelope) in four bands from 5e-13 to 0.2176 equals the mean Re lambda in each band for both solvers (DOP853 0.0371, 0.0510, 0.0613, 0.0698 against 0.0370, 0.0508, 0.0612, 0.0698 per tau; Radau 0.0402, 0.0531, 0.0630, 0.0713 against 0.0400, 0.0529, 0.0629, 0.0713). Level-crossing times: DOP853 rtol 1e-8 and 1e-12 cross every level from 1e-12 to the threshold at the same sample as rtol 1e-10 (lag 0.0 ms); Radau lags DOP853 by 380 ms at 1e-12, 286 ms at 1e-10, 210 ms at 1e-6, 177 ms at 1e-2, 181 ms at the threshold; the lag times the band growth rate gives ln(amplitude ratio) 1.06 to 1.41 (mean about 1.2) at all 13 levels, i.e. a nearly constant factor of about 3.3 over 11 decades of amplitude.
  Reading [reasoned, not tested]: Radau's trajectory is the DOP853 trajectory scaled by a constant factor of about 3 in amplitude (equivalently shifted 0.18 s in time at the end), the amplitude having been seeded at the double-precision floor, which differs between solvers; the 1 ms bound then cannot be expected to hold between two solvers for a noise-free headline whose onset is set by roundoff. Not shown: whether DOP853 itself moves by a comparable amount under a 1-ulp change of the start state; the pre-onset amplitude cannot be read from the stored float64 v below about 5e-15. Smallest extra run to settle it, PROPOSED, not run, for the reviewer's ruling: DOP853 rtol 1e-10, headline P2 linear 120 s, start state of run_mf (y0) with v shifted by +1 ulp (about 1.1e-16), and optionally -1 ulp; about 3 min each at the measured 178 s (DL-177); needs a short script calling run_mf(cfg, y0=...) (no config key exists). If the onset moves by the order of 0.1 s the 181 ms is within the roundoff sensitivity of the headline. An alternative that tests the Radau side is Radau at rtol 1e-9 or 1e-8 (cost UNVERIFIED; 26 min at rtol 1e-10, DL-178). Any amendment of the solver clause is a new departure for the user.

## DL-196  MS8 8f5: six reviewer rulings; stored-data burst diagnosis and clean-tree re-run of the 8f3 sets (label and reason)    [ID: MS8, 8f5, RB3, RB6, DL-189, DL-193, DL-195]
Date:            2026-10-18        Author:
Decision:        Rulings: (1) diagnose the deterministic pre-onset burst (34.575 to 36.053 s, peak 2.23e-5, identical to 8 digits in the three DOP853 headline runs, DL-193) from stored data only; the hypothesis TESTED, not assumed, is [reasoned, not tested], EXPLORATORY: the burst is seeded by the start of the J ramp on P2 at t_on + 0.25 T_ramp = 35 s (path_hypoxia, a derivative kink), the zero-phase band-pass spreads it earlier than 35 s, and the headline onset grows from this burst, not from the roundoff floor. (2) No Radau run at a looser rtol; a targeted Radau run is only PROPOSED after the diagnosis, for the reviewer's ruling. (3) Sets A (4 runs) and B (2 runs) of 8f3 are re-run from the committed tree so that the records show git dirty = false; onsets and stored arrays are compared bit for bit with the first runs; the first records stay on disk as SUPERSEDED, not deleted. (4) Every new script is committed before any simulation. (5) The pytest exit code is taken from pytest itself, not from a pipe, and reported. (6) The 8f4 supplementary runs (start distance 0.5 and 3) are included in the diagnosis as stored data; the observation to test, exploratory: the delay in eta units falls as the start distance rises (+0.172 at 0.5, +0.066 at 1.5, -0.065 at 3), opposite to entry-exit theory for a longer decay, which would fit an onset seeded by the burst rather than by the decaying delta0. No G6 verdict; no frozen criterion or evaluation rule changes; 8f4 records show git dirty = false, so no 8f4 re-run. Method: a burst is a contiguous run of the envelope (25 to 100 Hz band-pass, Hilbert, the one the raw crossing uses) above 1e-12 (the level the reviewer named); pre-onset means it ends before the raw first crossing of 0.217622; a path breakpoint has a burst if a pre-onset segment contains it (no window width assumed). The burst-seeded prediction reuses entry_exit unchanged and moves only the seed (amplitude A at time t_s, then A exp(I(t) - I(t_s)) = threshold); the required seed amplitude is log10(threshold) - (I(t_c) - I(t_s)) / ln 10. Code: src/mprsurge/analysis/rb_diag_burst.py, scripts/run_rb_diag_burst.py (analysis, writes the new results/A7/rb_diag_burst.json; no existing rb_eval or rb_diag file is touched), scripts/run_ms8_diag_rerun.py (integrates; imports scripts/run_ms8_diag_runs.py unchanged, target directory results/ms8_diag_rerun, refuses a dirty tree and a non-empty target). Label EXPLORATORY: post-hoc, outside S5, S13 and every rb_eval manifest, feeds no gate.

## DL-198  MS8 8f5: burst diagnosis from stored data (EXPLORATORY); the burst is a deterministic response at path breakpoints and the onset does not grow from it; rb_diag_burst.json sha256    [ID: MS8, 8f5, RB3, RB5, RB6, DL-189, DL-193, DL-195, DL-196, DL-197]
Date:            2026-10-18        Author:
Decision:        none; exploratory reading, no gate, no G6 verdict. Stored data only (no simulation in this entry). Burst = envelope above 1e-12 (DL-196). File results/A7/rb_diag_burst.json (new; rb_eval_ms8.json 96e9e51c..., rb_diag_ms8.json 3fb10f13..., rb_diag_exploratory.json 8a388a55..., rb_diag_startdist.json e16808cc... unchanged) sha256 a724b37eeddfd2eabf2391d05345f3578b28e949df65e0fa44fbaf4d9b960b39.
  (3a) Headline family, P2 linear 120 s, delta0 1e-6. There are two pre-onset bursts, not one: at t_on (4.570 to 5.470 s, peak 2.2214e-5 at 5.004 s) and at the J-ramp start (34.575 to 36.053 s, peak 2.2299e-5 at 35.009 s); a third follows the onset at the J-ramp end (154.577 to 156.325 s, peak 6.55e-5 at 155.008 s). Each contains a path breakpoint (corners of ramps.make_path; the integrator is restarted there). DOP853 rtol 1e-8 / 1e-10 / 1e-12: start, end and peak time of both pre-onset bursts identical to the sample; J-start peak 2.22994905133e-5 / 2.22994905137e-5 / 2.22994905141e-5 (relative spread 3.7e-11; t_on burst 5.1e-11); onset 58.698 s in all three; the growth segment (envelope above 1e-12) starts at 53.763 s in all three. Radau 1e-10: same burst times, J-start peak 2.22994897590e-5, Radau / DOP853 = 0.99999996616 (t_on burst 0.99999999032); onset 58.879 s (+0.181 s, recomputed from the stored records); growth segment starts 54.143 s (+0.380 s). Growth rate of ln(envelope) over the last decade before the crossing (existing rb_diag definition): DOP853 7.2079 per s, Radau 7.3451 per s. Implied onset shift -ln(0.99999996616) / 7.2079 = +4.7e-9 s against the observed +0.181 s (ratio 2.6e-8). The seed ratio that would give 0.181 s is exp(-7.2079 x 0.181) = 0.271. Envelope median between the end of the t_on burst and the start of the J burst 1.82e-15, between the end of the J burst and the start of the growth segment 2.07e-15: the envelope is back at the floor level after each burst.
  (3b) 26 noise-free P2 S5 runs. Linear, T_ramp 31.6 to 1000 s (7 values): the J-start burst is a lone pre-onset burst whose peak is 8 to 9 ms after the breakpoint t_on + 0.25 T_ramp (12.906 to 255.000 s), a lag that does not change while the breakpoint moves by a factor of 20; peak x T_ramp = 2.68e-3 s at all seven (peak 8.47e-5 at T 31.6, 2.67e-6 at T 1000). Sigmoid, T_ramp 5.6 to 1000 s (10 values): peak 4 to 5 ms after the breakpoint, peak x T_ramp = 1.08e-4 s at all ten. So the burst time tracks t_on + 0.25 T_ramp, the amplitude scales as 1/T_ramp, and the sigmoid burst is 0.040 of the linear one (t_on burst: 0.053 to 0.066). Not separable (the J-start breakpoint lies in the growth segment or in a segment with the other breakpoints): linear T_ramp 1 to 17.8 s, sigmoid T_ramp 1 to 3.2 s. The t_on burst is lone in the same runs from T_ramp 5.6 s (linear) with peak x T_ramp 2.26e-3 to 2.73e-3 s and a peak 4 to 6 ms after t_on. No pre-onset segment without a breakpoint exists in any of the 26 runs. p2_sigmoid T_ramp 1 s has no raw crossing (onset None, as in the A7 table).
  (3c) Noise-free P5 (26 runs): a lone burst at t_on in 23 runs (all but linear T_ramp 1 and 1.78 s and sigmoid 1 s), peak 4 ms after t_on (6 ms at T 1000), peak x T_ramp 2.7e-3 s linear (2.26e-3 at T 1000) and 1.8e-4 s sigmoid; a burst of about the same size at the last breakpoint t_on + 2 T_ramp, after the onset, where it is separable. Noise-free P1 (26 runs): not separable: the envelope is above 1e-12 from t = 0 to the onset in every run (the growth segment starts at 0.0 s), so a t_on burst cannot be told from the continuing envelope; the same holds for the 26 p1_start_distance runs. The P1 question "is there a burst at t_on" is therefore not answered by the stored data.
  (3d) delta0 1e-9 / 1e-6 / 1e-3: J-start burst peak 2.22994905142e-5 / 2.22994905137e-5 / 2.22994905147e-5 (independent of delta0 to 10 digits), at 35.009 s; onset 58.698 s for all three. The t_on burst does depend on delta0: peak 2.271e-5 / 2.221e-5 / 5.153e-4 (the delta0 transient adds to the response at the kink).
  (3e) Burst-seeded entry-exit (existing A7 eigenvalue integral, only the seed moved), headline: seed at the J-start burst (35.009 s, 2.2299e-5): t_pred 68.337 s, eta_pred 3.2434, predicted delay 0.3473, against observed onset 58.698 s and delay 0.0662: onset minus t_pred -9.639 s, 11.25 A4 steps (|eta at onset - eta at t_pred| / 0.025). Seed at the t_on burst: t_pred 115.054 s (-56.356 s, 65.75 steps). A7 as built (delta0 1e-6 at t_on): 115.225 s (-56.527 s, 65.95 steps). Net gain I(58.698 s) - I(35.009 s) = -96.999: the burst is damped by e^-97 (about 1e-42) before the observed onset; the amplitude at 35.009 s that would give the observed onset is 10^41.46 against the actual 10^-4.65 (46.1 decades more than the burst). For delta0 at t_on the amplitude needed is 10^473.3 against 10^-6.
  (3f) Start distance 0.5 / 1.5 / 3 (class D-tr in all; onset 37.260 / 58.698 / 75.448 s; delay in eta +0.17208 / +0.06619 / -0.06467): growth segment starts 33.316 / 53.763 / 71.066 s, growth rate 4.342 / 7.208 / 8.027 per s. J-start burst: at 0.5 not separable, the growth segment starts 1.7 s BEFORE the J ramp starts (35 s), so the J-ramp start cannot be the seed of that onset; at 1.5 peak 2.2299e-5; at 3 peak 8.986e-6 at 35.003 s. t_on burst: 2.500e-5 at 5.019 s / 2.221e-5 at 5.004 s / 2.028e-5 at 5.002 s. Predictions (onset minus t_pred; A4 steps; predicted delay): 0.5, seed t_on burst: t_pred 52.579 s (-15.319 s, 12.77 steps, delay +0.4912; A7 as built 52.823 s, +0.4963); 1.5, seed J-start burst: 68.337 s (-9.639 s, 11.25 steps, +0.3473); 3, seed J-start burst: 126.530 s (-51.082 s; the step count 82.6 is not meaningful because t_pred is after the eta ramp ends at 125 s, where eta is constant; predicted delay +2.0; the amplitude needed is about 394 decades above the burst); 3, A7 as built and t_on burst seed: no t_pred.
  What the data support: (i) the burst is a deterministic feature of the integrated solution at path breakpoints, a few ms after the breakpoint, with an amplitude proportional to 1/T_ramp and to the slope jump of the profile, independent of delta0 (J-start burst), of the DOP853 rtol (1e-8 to 1e-12) and of the solver (Radau within 3.4e-8 relative); it is not roundoff. (ii) Its time tracks t_on + 0.25 T_ramp; it also appears at t_on and at the last breakpoint, so it is not specific to the J ramp. (iii) The envelope returns to the floor level after it. What the data do not support: that the headline onset grows from the burst. The linear gain from the burst to the observed onset is e^-97; the burst-seeded prediction is 9.6 s (11 A4 steps) late (A7 as built: 56.5 s, 66 steps), and needs a seed 46 decades above the burst; Radau shares the burst to 3.4e-8 and still shifts the onset by 181 ms (implied 5 ns) and the growth segment by 380 ms; at start distance 0.5 the growth starts before the J ramp. The onset does not depend on delta0 over six decades, which fits a floor-seeded onset and is not evidence against it. So the DL-189 reading (onset set from the floor, which differs between solvers) is neither confirmed nor excluded here; it is the remaining reading [reasoned, not tested]. Observation 6 (delay in eta falls with start distance): reproduced from stored data; the burst-seeded predictions do not reproduce it (predicted delays 0.49, 0.35, 2.0 at 0.5, 1.5, 3 from the available seeds, not falling), so the falling trend is not explained by a burst seed. Not shown: the physical cause of the burst. An amplitude of constant x 1/T_ramp that is independent of rtol and solver is consistent with the response of the exact solution to a slope discontinuity of eta(t) or J(t) [reasoned, not tested; no run with a smoothed path exists]; a solver-restart effect is not excluded by the stored data.

## DL-202  MS8 8f6: effective seed against the ramp-kink burst, stored data only (EXPLORATORY)    [ID: MS8, 8f6, RB3, DL-198, DL-200]
Date:            2026-10-18        Author:
Decision:        none; exploratory, no gate, no G6 verdict. Effective seed = threshold x exp(-(I(t_c) - I(t_on))) with threshold 0.217622 = 0.1 x A_ref (A_ref 2.176222) and I the existing entry_exit integral of Re lambda (path_gain, A4 grid step 0.025), t_c the observed raw crossing. 13 runs: the 9 in-range S5 runs and the 4 Set A clean re-runs (git dirty = false). Effective seed (T_ramp s; delta0; start distance): P1 linear (1; 1e-6; 1.5) 1.557e-2; P1 linear (1.778; 1e-6; 1.5) 8.19e-3; P1 sigmoid (1; 1e-6; 1.5) 7.27e-3; P1 start-distance linear (1; 1e-6; 0.5) 7.07e-3, (1.778) 3.73e-3, (3.162) 2.09e-3, (5.623) 1.14e-3, (10) 6.70e-4; P5 linear (1.778; 1e-6; 1.5) 8.40e-3; Set A (0.5): T 1 s delta0 1e-9 7.07e-3, 1e-3 6.11e-3; T 10 s delta0 1e-9 6.70e-4, 1e-3 2.90e-4. Burst peak and ratio: NOT SEPARABLE in all 13. In the 12 P1 runs the envelope is above 1e-12 from t = 0 to the onset (growth segment 0 to 16 to 25 s), so a burst at t_on cannot be told from the continuing envelope; in the P5 run the t_on burst lies in the growth segment (4.459 to 9.137 s). So no measured ratio effective seed / burst peak exists, and the question whether the ratio is roughly constant across T_ramp cannot be answered from stored data: the effective seed itself falls from 1.6e-2 to 6.7e-4 as T_ramp goes 1 to 10 s (start distance 0.5: 7.1e-3, 3.7e-3, 2.1e-3, 1.1e-3, 6.7e-4, a factor 10.6 over a factor 10 in T_ramp), while the burst peak, where separable, scales as 1/T_ramp (peak x T_ramp 2.26e-3 to 2.74e-3 s for the lone t_on bursts of 11 P5 linear runs). Observation (descriptive): the effective seed at start distance 0.5 falls about as 1/T_ramp; whether that is a coincidence of the entry-exit gain is not tested. Ratio delta0 / effective seed at delta0 1e-6 is 6.4e-5 to 1.5e-3 (the observed onsets are earlier than delta0 seeding would give, as in the 8f2 offsets), and the Set A onset (and so the effective seed) is the same for delta0 1e-9 and 1e-6 (DL-192). P5 linear T_ramp 1.778 s, burst-seeded prediction with the burst amplitude EXTRAPOLATED [reasoned, UNVERIFIED]: amplitude = median(peak x T_ramp) 2.698e-3 s of the 11 lone t_on bursts of the other P5 linear runs, divided by T_ramp = 1.517e-3, seeded at t_on + median lag 4 ms = 5.004 s; predicted onset t_pred 6.872 s (eta_pred 4.7107, delay +1.8146) against observed raw crossing 6.825 s (eta 4.8041): onset minus t_pred -0.047 s, 3.74 A4 steps (0.025); A7 as built (delta0 1e-6 at t_on): t_pred 7.143 s, observed minus t_pred -0.318 s. Extrapolated ratio effective seed / burst amplitude 8.404e-3 / 1.517e-3 = 5.54 (not a measured ratio). Limits: the extrapolated amplitude comes from other T_ramp values and the burst itself is not separable at 1.778 s; one run only.

Chosen:          -   Default from: DL-200

## DL-226  MS9 9c PART 1: decomposition of the NC1 network S+ on the stored record (no simulation); A8 sensitivity variants post-hoc    [ID: MS9, 9c, A8, G7, A10, NC1, D5, D6, D8, DL-220, DL-221, DL-225]
Date:            2026-10-19        Author:
Decision:        FACTS ONLY; no threshold and no frozen criterion changed; run by scripts/analyse_nc1_net.py part1 (committed first) on results/S12/NC1_net/NC1_net_0000_1a8cb131785a (npz sha256 93496429...). (1) Signal: the classifier reads npz['v'], the bin-end mean V over the non-refractory neurons (exclude_refractory = true), not the binned rate r; fs 1 kHz; W = 2 s, step 1 s; record 0.001 to 135 s, t_on 5 s. (2) Baseline = the windows lying wholly in [t_on - 5, t_on] = [0, 5] s: 4 windows (centres 1 to 4 s; the 2 s discard is before t = 0, so these are 2 to 7 s after integration start). P_G mean 1.781e-4 (min 1.395e-4, max 2.021e-4, max/min 1.449); P_non-G mean 2.102e-4 (max/min 1.415); odds P_G/P_non-G mean 0.8704 (0.614 to 1.182, max/min 1.924). (3) Ratios against the factor 2.0 (rel = odds / baseline odds, abs = P_G / baseline P_G): 130 windows after t_on; rel median 1.46, 90th percentile 1.98, max 3.11 (t_c 25 s); abs median 0.93, 90th 1.89, max 2.55 (t_c 26 s); windows >= 2: rel 13, abs 10; >= 4: none. The classifier's episode is the run of window centres 14, 15, 16 s: windows 14 and 16 are flagged (rel 2.090 and 2.289, abs 2.039 and 2.269: margins 1.045 x, 1.145 x and 1.020 x, 1.134 x the factor), window 15 is NOT flagged (rel 1.534, abs 1.783); the gap of one unflagged window (1 s) is shorter than W = 2 s and is merged. Later flagged runs (centres): rel 19 to 20, 25 to 31 (peak 3.11 at 25 s), 45 to 47, 53; abs 19 to 21, 24 to 27, 30. (4) Episode: onset 14.0 s (centre of the first flagged window), end 16.5 s, class S+ because the rel and abs episodes share a window (O10), terminated, peak window f_pk 41.5 Hz (t_c 16 s), peak_rho 0.666. Window f_pk (argmax of the PSD in 25 to 100 Hz, resolution 0.5 Hz): 62, 58.5, 57, 80.5, 78, 50.5, 95, 47, 45.5 at t_c 5 to 13 s, then 44, 42.5, 41.5, 40, 39, 38, 37, 36, 35, 34, 33, 32, 31, 30, 29, 28, 27, 26 at t_c 14 to 31 s (a steady fall of 1 Hz per s), then 39.5, 38.5, 37.5, 37 and scattered values after 36 s. (5) RECONCILIATION of 128 cycles, 41.5 Hz and 2.5 s: duration = (windows in the run) x step = 3 x 1 s = 3.0 s; cycles = duration x MEAN of the windows' f_pk = 3.0 x (44.0 + 42.5 + 41.5) / 3 = 3.0 x 42.667 = 128.0; 41.5 Hz is the f_pk of the PEAK-power window only; onset is the CENTRE of the first window and end is the centre of the last window + step / 2, so end - onset = 16.5 - 14.0 = 2.5 s = duration - step / 2; the data the three windows touch are 13 to 17 s (4.0 s); the cycle count is not a phase count. An independent count of the unwrapped phase of the 25 to 100 Hz band-passed v (ours, comparison only): 136.2 cycles over onset..end and 229.7 over 13 to 17 s (a broadband phase advances at a mean rate above the 42.7 Hz spectral peak). A consequence of the formula (arithmetic, not measured): at W = 2 s, step 1 s, one flagged window already counts step x f_pk >= 1 s x 25 Hz = 25 cycles >= 10, so min_cycles = 10 cannot reject a single flagged window whose f_pk is in the band. (6) D8 on this record: the fit window starts at the first sample of the band-passed (25 to 100 Hz) Hilbert envelope >= 0.1 x A_ref = 0.217622 after t_on; THE ENVELOPE NEVER REACHES IT: 0 samples, rate and SE nan, t_start nan, 0 cycles; by the frozen rule (nan compares False) the call is "non-damped". The D8 test therefore did not filter this episode, and the A_min factors 0.05 and 0.2 change nothing here (the fit stays undefined; baseline v sd 0.038, the mean-field A_ref 2.176 is the reference of D7). (7) Context at the episode (t = 14 to 17 s): mean rate 7.07 Hz (baseline 7.98 Hz, sd of the 1 ms rate 0.8 Hz, whole record after t_on 4.42 Hz); mean v -0.649; eta-bar(t) = 1.097 (1.134 at 14 s, 1.075 at 16 s; eta had fallen by 0.30 of the 3.50 total); eta_H (A4, J0 -21, Delta 0.3, tau_d 5 ms) = 2.896046, Hopf frequency 32.01 Hz; distance eta-bar - eta_H = -1.80 (the stable side; -1.50 at the start state); A4 leading Re lambda at the episode time -65.2 per s (-0.652 per tau), complex pair at 25.3 Hz; at the start state -51.0 per s (26.35 Hz); mean-field fixed-point rate there 7.1 Hz, network window mean rate 7.1 Hz. Re lambda is negative along the whole path (-51 at t_on to -214 per s). The A4 linearisation is the mean-field one (N = infinity); the network has N = 1e4. (8) A8 sensitivity variants on this record, POST-HOC, feed no gate (class, onset to end, cycles, f_pk; same classifier code and variant set as configs/A8_sensitivity.yaml): V0 S+ 14.0 to 16.5, 128 cycles, 41.5 Hz; band 30 to 120 Hz: S+ 19.0 to 20.5 (75 cycles, 38 Hz); factor 1.5: S-abs 7.0 to 7.5 (rel and abs episodes do not overlap, O10); factor 4: NS (rel max 3.11, abs max 2.55 < 4); A_min 0.05 and 0.2: S+ unchanged (D8 undefined in both); window x0.5 (W 1 s): S+ 12.5 to 14.75 (118.5 cycles, 43 Hz; 9 baseline windows); window x2 (W 4 s): S+ 20 to 21 (74 cycles, 37 Hz; ONE baseline window); minimum cycles 5 and 20: S+ unchanged. 9 of 10 variants (V0 included) give a surge class; only factor 4 gives NS. (9) Outputs (git-ignored): results/ms9/9c/nc1_net_variants.csv (cac69254...), nc1_net_windows.csv (207e5876...).

Clause 1 ("every onset is S-sus or D-sus") also fails: 26 of 27 mode-D P2 runs and 760 of 900 map-1 cells are D-tr. RECOMMENDATION: G3 NOT TRIGGERED (the plan's expectation, Table 4.2). Mode-N S-sus (44 of 130 S5 P2 mode-N runs, 829 of 2,250 subgrid runs) is a reported caveat and cannot trigger G3 (reviewer's ruling; no further reading is added here). The statement "G3 not triggered" is made at the MS9 close.

## DL-286  MS10 10b: Gaussian and uniform heterogeneity built; tests    [ID: MS10, 10b, M10-13, D28, D29, S10, DL-282]
Date:            2026-10-23        Author:
Decision:        FACT. heterogeneity_offsets(N, dist, sampling, rng) added to src/mprsurge/qif_network.py (scipy.special.ndtri, outside the Numba kernel); lorentzian_offsets unchanged and called for het_dist lorentzian; the two ConfigError guards 'S10 shapes are not built' removed; gaussian/uniform with het_sampling random raise ConfigError (the random variant is stated for the Lorentzian only; not ruled). The Numba kernel qif_chunk is untouched (git diff shows no line of it), so no re-time is needed (9.2 step 4). Tests: (a) SHA-256 of the Lorentzian offsets for N 1e3 and 1e4 equal the pre-change values (7274d920..., a104bc97...); (b) sorted and symmetric (N 7, 1000, 10001, all three shapes); (c) Gaussian: sd*sqrt(2 ln 2) - 1 = -1.04e-4 at N 1e5 (-8.2e-4 at 1e4), pdf(1)/pdf(0) - 0.5 = -7.2e-5 at N 1e5 (relative error 1.4e-4), histogram density ratio at q = 1 over q = 0 is 0.5004; uniform: max |q| = (N-1)/(N+1) = 1 - 2/(N+1) (0.99998 at N 1e5), spacing 2/(N+1); (d) a Delta ramp keeps q fixed; (e) N = 200 networks run for all three shapes, mean of eta_j equals eta_bar to 1e-12. INCONSISTENCY in the 10b prompt: it states max |q| = 1 - 1/(N+1); R6 gives u_N = N/(N+1), so q_N = 2u_N - 1 = 1 - 2/(N+1). The test uses the R6 value. Finite-N bias: the quantile Gaussian lacks the tails beyond u = 1/(N+1), so its sample sd is 0.08 percent below the continuous value at N 1e4.

Date:            2026-10-24        Author:
Decision:        RULING (the 10d answer, recorded). E-2: a seed whose f_pk or onset is undefined for the comparison fails that test (reported "undefined"). ## DL-312  MS10 10e R27: the network onset is the classifier onset; time-origin check (amends R2 and R23 for network records)    [ID: MS10, 10e, R27, E-1, R2, R23, RB1]
Date:            2026-10-24        Author:
Decision:        RULING AND FACT. R2 and R23 assumed a raw-crossing onset field for network records; the frozen mode-N classifier outputs only ClassResult.episode.onset_s (centre of the first flagged spectrogram window; the earlier of the relative and absolute episodes after the minimum-cycle and D8 tests). For RB1 the network onset is that classifier onset (window centre, Conventions.onset default), compared with the stored mode-D mean-field raw-crossing onset; tolerance one spectrogram step (Table 2.1), inclusive (E-3). The evaluator's own raw-crossing reading (first time the band-passed Hilbert envelope of the network v reaches 0.1 x A_ref) is secondary and post hoc: reported, feeds no gate, "undefined" allowed. Mode-D classification and RB3 readings unchanged. TIME ORIGINS (stated before any network record was read; check_time_origin, origin_check_all): classifier onset of a network record = window centre in seconds of sample index / 1000, v starting at path time 0 with the 2 s discard removed (qif_network.run_network), sample i = mean over the 1 ms bin [i, i+1) ms stamped at the bin end (first stamp 1 ms, path time of sample 0 = 0 ms). Mean-field onset (stored raw crossing, mode D) = sample index / 1000 in a record whose t_ms starts at 0 ms (sample i = state at i ms; path time of sample 0 = 0 ms). Both: t_on 5 s, interval 1 ms, the same path clock; stamp offset 1 ms (bin end against instant), reported, below every tolerance in use (smallest step 1/6 s). Checked against the 2 stored references (T_ramp 10 s and 120 s) and the 5 companion records, for the network configs of S8, S9, S10 and the controls: shared = true in all 7 comparisons. The evaluator stops (EvalRefused, "STOP (R27)") on a mismatch of t_on, sample interval or path time of sample 0, and when a network record's t_ms does not start at one bin.
Reason:          instruction of the reviewer (10e prompt, R27).

Chosen:          as ruled   Default from: -

## DL-340  MS11 11b: does the S4 up/down record count as an RB5 up-versus-down result? facts and a recommendation, NOT decided    [ID: MS11, 11b, RB5, S4, P5, DL-127, DL-128]
Date:            2026-10-26        Author:
Decision:        NOT DECIDED (for the reviewer). RB5 text (Table 7.2): "up vs down ramps (P5, S4)"; criterion "Class unchanged. Delay shifts are the expected memory effect and are reported". Facts: (1) S4 (Table 6.2) is the quasi-static sweep, eta_bar from eta_H - 2 to eta_H + 4, 61 steps up then down, 2 s each, last 1 s read, state carried between steps, delta0 on v at the start of each step (configs/S4.yaml; mean field at ref_devalle, network at 15 steps; DL-127, DL-128). (2) Its result is an amplitude and frequency comparison of the up and down branches, not a Table 2.1 class: at ref_devalle up and down agree to 3e-4 relative or better from eta_bar 3.096 to 6.9; next to eta_H the branches differ (2.896: 0.0760 up, 0.5511 down), read in DL-127 as the 2 s step against critical slowing, not a persistent hysteresis loop; at ref_ceni up and down agree to 2e-7. (3) The S4 steps are constant-parameter holds, not ramps with T_ramp, onset or delay; no class was computed for them. (4) The P5 up/down ramps (S5, MS8) are classified runs and are logged as the RB5 up/down result (docs/ms11_plan.md section 4.1). (5) The MS8 close does not restate S4 as an RB5 result (docs/ms11_plan.md section 4.1; UNVERIFIED). Recommendation: use P5 as the RB5 up-versus-down result (it is the only one with a class), report the S4 branch agreement beside it as quasi-static supporting evidence labelled "no class, constant-parameter steps", and do not count S4 toward the "class unchanged" criterion. Open field rb5_updown_source in configs/ms11/ms11_eval.yaml (proposal P5_with_S4_reported_beside; the alternatives are P5_only and P5_and_S4_quasi_static).

## DL-341  MS11 11b: what the existing RB9(a) unit-level test compares (facts; no ruling on whether it counts)    [ID: MS11, 11b, RB9, DL-061, M11-8]
Date:            2026-10-26        Author:
Decision:        FACT (read from tests/test_units.py::test_rb9a_dimensional_and_nondimensional_runs_agree_within_half_a_percent; the test was not run for this entry). It is parametrized on tau_ms 10 and 20. It resolves a config with model.tau_ms set, path_eta (eta_start 1.0, eta_peak 4.0), T_ramp 1 s, t_on 0.5 s, baseline 0.5 s, hold 0.5 s (the other values from configs/base.yaml, M3 at ref_devalle values), runs the non-dimensional mean field in memory (S.run_mf(cfg)["arrays"]; no run record is written), and integrates the dimensional right-hand side of plan 3.1 (t in ms, r in 1/ms; tau dr/dt = Delta/(pi tau) + 2 r v, tau dv/dt = v^2 + eta + J tau s + I - (pi tau r)^2, tau_d ds/dt = -s + r) with scipy DOP853, rtol 1e-10, atol 1e-13, max_step 0.5 tau, from the same stable fixed point with delta0 added at t_on. Compared quantities: r times tau, v, s times tau, on the 1 ms output grid. Metric: the maximum absolute difference over the run divided by the maximum absolute value of that variable. Tolerance: 0.5 percent (0.005) for each of the three variables (strict less-than), stated as test-level (DL-061). It is not a run on the headline path (P2, T_ramp 120 s), it does not use a full run record, and it is not logged as an RB9 result. No ruling is made on whether it counts as RB9(a); the field rb9a_source is open.

## DL-357  MS11 11c: ruling 12 rb9d_runs = YES (small list MS11_RB9D, reported only); parameter specification AMBIGUOUS, item STOPPED, question to the reviewer    [ID: MS11, 11c, RB9, RB9d, rb9d_runs, M11-8]
Date:            2026-10-26        Author:
Decision:        RULED and STOPPED. Ruling 12: YES, add a small list MS11_RB9D with the two tau +-20 percent runs on the headline cell, reported only; state what is held fixed and what changes before writing it; if ambiguous, STOP on this item. YES is recorded (rb9d_runs = separate_post_hoc_list). The list is NOT written. FACTS. Plan Table 7.2 RB9(d): "tau +-20%", "reported only, since every gamma result the reports cite fixes tau = 10 ms"; the plan says nothing about what is held. Code: model.tau_ms (Table 3.2: fixed, 10 ms) enters only through (1) the conversion of every duration given in seconds into tau units (ramps.make_path: T_ramp_s, t_on_s, I_period_s; simulate_mf: baseline, hold, discard), (2) the synaptic ratio tau_d/tau = ms_to_tau(model.tau_d_ms, model.tau_ms), tau_d_ms being a separate parameter in ms (5 ms at the headline), and (3) the output stamps t_ms = t_tau * tau_ms. eta_start, eta_peak, J, Delta and I are dimensionless numbers and do not change with tau_ms; path.eta_H is a stored number (2.8960461989737856, the A4 Hopf value at tau_d/tau = 0.5) from which resolve_config derives eta_start = eta_H - 1.5 and eta_peak = max(4, eta_H + 2); it is not recomputed from tau. The classifier works on the 1 kHz output in Hz with the frozen 25 to 100 Hz band and the frozen threshold 0.1 x A_ref (A_ref measured at tau 10 ms, tau_d 5 ms). So a bare override model.tau_ms = 8 or 12 gives reading (A) below. AMBIGUITY (three readings): (A) tau_d_ms held at 5 ms and all durations held in seconds: tau_d/tau becomes 0.625 and 0.4167, the Hopf point of the path moves while the eta numbers are held (the start is no longer eta_H - 1.5 of the new system), the 120 s ramp is 15,000 / 10,000 tau instead of 12,000; this is a genuine parameter test of the ratio. (B) tau_d scaled with tau (tau_d_ms = 4 and 6, ratio 0.5 held) and durations held in seconds: the Hopf eta is unchanged, frequencies in Hz scale by 1/tau (x1.25, x0.833), the ramp is 15,000 / 10,000 tau. (C) B with the durations also scaled with tau: the non-dimensional run is identical and only the ms and Hz labels change (a trivial result). QUESTIONS for the reviewer: (1) A, B or C? (2) eta numbers held at the headline values (the code default) or re-derived from a Hopf point at the new tau_d/tau (that needs an A4 continuation at each tau, which is a new computation, not in the plan)? (3) the frozen classifier band and threshold unchanged (the default)? (4) which quantities are reported (class, onset, f_pk in Hz and in units of 1/tau, delay against the headline eta_H)? RECOMMENDATION (not a ruling): (A) with eta numbers, band and threshold held, because the plan's parameter table fixes tau_d in ms and the check is of tau alone; report class, onset, delay (against eta_H = 2.896, labelled) and f_pk in Hz and in cycles per tau. Deterministic runs (kind mf, seeds.spawn_key null in configs/base.yaml) use no noise stream: NO new seed key is needed, confirmed; the key family [11, ...] is untouched. Run count if added: 236 + 2 = 238; provisional timing in DL-363.

## DL-369  MS11 11d: ruling 2d and step 4: recompute hooks of the 26 carried checks coded, tested on synthetic fixtures only    [ID: MS11, 11d, A11, RB1, RB2, RB3, RB4, RB5, RB6, RB8, G5, G6, G7, sigma_check]
Date:            2026-10-26        Author:
Decision:        FACT. src/mprsurge/analysis/ms11_hooks.py: 26 hooks, one per row of a11_logged (check_registry stops A11 if the two sets differ): MS8 14 (RB3 a_inrange_runs, a_headline, b_raw_crossing, b_classifier_onset, c_T_ramp_56_to_316, d_profile; RB5 delta0_headline_class, delta0_headline_delay, start_distance; RB6 heun_headline, solver_class_headline, solver_onset_headline, rtol_headline; G6 gate), MS9 4 (RB2 noisy_subgrid_agreement, RB4 parameter_perturbation, G5, G7), MS10 7 (RB1 headline_10s, headline_120s, cells_30s, n_rule_60s, overall; RB8 heterogeneity; sigma_check) and 1 from the frozen leaf (RB8 m4_adaptation: OPEN while RB8.M4_criteria has no value). Each reads stored data only through a Context (RealContext for the real run, built by scripts/run_A11.py) and returns the recomputed verdict WORD in the logged vocabulary; A11 maps it with the same table, compares it with the logged word, and writes any difference (word and status) in the note column; a recomputed word with no table entry gives NOT EVALUABLE with the word kept and flagged; an exception in a hook propagates. Registered keys: RB3/a_inrange_runs; RB3/a_headline; RB3/b_raw_crossing; RB3/b_classifier_onset; RB3/c_T_ramp_56_to_316; RB3/d_profile; RB5/delta0_headline_class; RB5/delta0_headline_delay; RB5/start_distance; RB6/heun_headline; RB6/solver_class_headline; RB6/solver_onset_headline; RB6/rtol_headline; G6/gate; RB2/noisy_subgrid_agreement; RB4/parameter_perturbation; G5/gate; G7/gate; RB1/headline_10s; RB1/headline_120s; RB1/cells_30s; RB1/n_rule_60s; RB1/overall; RB8/heterogeneity; sigma_check/S8_baseline_std; RB8/m4_adaptation. WHAT EACH SHARES WITH THE ORIGINAL EVALUATION (independence is NOT claimed): all 26 read the thresholds through the criteria loader; every hook that uses a class uses the class written by the frozen classifier (surge_metrics); the 14 MS8 hooks call the same rb_eval functions that made the logged verdicts, on the A7 table that the a7 pieces wrote; the 7 MS10 hooks call the same ms10_eval functions and read the records through ms10_eval.read_lists with table21 = True, which calls the 9i function (ms9_9i.j_exit_static_path); the 4 MS9 hooks re-derive the verdict from the stored class tables (s16_classes, subgrid_classes, map1_classes, nc1_classes) by the plain definitions (M9-14, RB4, G5, G7) written anew, but read the class column the frozen classifier wrote, and use no 9i function; the M4 hook shares only the criteria loader. G6 is recomputed by applying the logged departure register (G6-D1 for RB3(a) in range, gate departure 3 for RB3(a) at the headline, G6-D2 for the solver onset, G6-D3 for the classifier-onset reading of RB3(b)) to the recomputed components: PASSED if every component MEETS, PASSED WITH DEPARTURES if every failing component is covered, NOT PASSED otherwise; the register is the reviewer's ruling (DL-208) and is applied, not recomputed. The independent recomputations of 8g, 9j and 10g are separate code paths and are not used. NOT RUN on any real record: tests use synthetic tables (the MS10 hooks drive the real ms10_eval functions on the 10d fake runs). RealContext opens nothing at construction. scripts/run_A11.py runs the hooks at the A11 evaluation step (--no-hooks leaves the rows carried and is used only by the fabricated-record test).

## DL-378  MS11 11e: the MS10 reader path of RealContext tested on FABRICATED records; one access gap fixed in code, one layout mismatch fixed in the fabricator    [ID: MS11, 11e, A11, DL-373, DL-369]
Date:            2026-10-26        Author:
Decision:        FACT. The MS10 reader path (ms10_eval.read_lists on the 103 network records of S8, S9, S10, C2_S8, C2_S9, C2_S10; the 5 MF_COMPANION records; the stored mean-field references of T_ramp 10 s and 120 s; origin_check_all) is exercised by the 7 MS10 hooks and by scripts/run_A11.py on FABRICATED records, in pytest's temporary folder outside results/, labelled 'fabricated' in the message and flags of every record (tests/fabricate_ms11.py, ms10_records), written with the real writers and the names and config hashes of the rows of the frozen MS10 lists, never evaluated as results and deleted with the temporary folder. The two stored references are the fabricated S5 records of the existing 11d tree. Tests (slow, full suite): tests/test_ms11_fabricated.py::test_the_ms10_reader_path_reads_103_fabricated_network_records_in_the_real_layout, test_the_ms10_reader_refuses_a_fabricated_network_record_with_the_old_t_ms_layout, test_the_seven_ms10_hooks_run_through_the_real_context_on_the_fabricated_records, test_run_a11_with_all_26_hooks_on_the_fabricated_tree_including_the_ms10_records (all 26 carried rows recomputed through run_A11.py with the 26 hooks). MISMATCH 1 (code, fixed): the MS10 path of RealContext ignored results_root: ms10_eval.read_lists, mf_references and origin_check_all read the repository results/ only (and mf_references verifies the stored references' SHA-256 against the real files), so a run of the hooks on a redirected tree would have read the REAL stored MS10 records. Fixed with an optional results_root (default None: behaviour unchanged) in ms10_eval.read_lists, mf_references, origin_check_all and the new redirect_rows; with a redirect the SHA-256 check of the stored references is skipped (their hashes belong to the real files); RealContext.ms10 passes the redirect only when its results root is not <repo>/results. MISMATCH 2 (fabricator, fixed): the 11d fabricated network series had t_ms starting at 0; the real network layout (qif_network.run_network) has t_ms at the bin END, (b + 1) bin, and the raster arrays; the R27 check refuses the old layout. The fabricator now writes the real layout for network records. No mismatch in the stored-evaluator code itself. To see the real layout, one header of one real stored network npz (results/S8/S8_head: array names, shapes and the first three t_ms values) was read; no hook, evaluator or classifier was run on any real record. The word values of the hooks on fabricated records are meaningless (made-up series) and are not recorded.

## DL-400  MS11 11g: independent recomputation STOPPED on an error in the independent script; nothing patched, nothing re-run    [ID: MS11, 11g, A11, RB6]
Date:            2026-10-27        Author:
Decision:        FACT, STOP (prompt step 5: an error stops the step). scripts/ms11_independent_check.py (commit 8ff8ee3) was run once on the real records (criteria gate ok; 254 stored records classified by the frozen classifier; map cells not yet reached). It raised ValueError at the network RB6 reading (ii), in my own welch_argmax (scipy.signal.welch): "noverlap=166 must be less than nperseg=85", after the warning "nperseg=333 is greater than signal length 85". Cause: the classifier episode of a network seed at dt 1e-3 is 85 samples (85 ms) long, shorter than the Table 2.1 window W = 0.333 s (333 samples) of the 10 s ramp, so a Welch average of W-long Hann windows cannot be formed inside the episode. The rules text (ms11_eval_rules.md section 3: "argmax of the PSD of v in 25 to 100 Hz (O6, resolution 1/W, no interpolation) over the window of the classifier episode") does not say how a window longer than the episode is handled; my reading (windows of length W lying inside the episode, averaged) was too narrow. The error is in the independent code path, not in A11; no A11 value was compared with an independent value for any row (the script stopped before any comparison and wrote no output file; results/A11 has only the three original files). No patch of either code path, no re-run, no diagnostic. Needs the reviewer: (a) rule how the reading (ii) PSD is to be formed when the episode is shorter than W (for example the spectrogram windows that overlap the episode, as the classifier's own episode f_pk rule, or one window of length W centred on the episode), after which the independent script is amended, committed and run once; or (b) record reading (ii) as not independently recomputable and run the other rows without it (which also needs an amended script). Which reading A11 used was not looked up (that would be reading the original code path for the answer).

## DL-401  MS11 11g: ruling on DL-400 (option a); how A11 forms RB6 network reading (ii) f_pk, in words; rules gap; candidate MS11-C8    [ID: MS11, 11g, A11, RB6, MS11-C8, DL-400]
Date:            2026-10-27        Author:
Decision:        RULED by the reviewer (11g resume prompt, step 2a): option (a); read, read-only and for that one point only, how A11 forms the reading (ii) f_pk when the classifier episode is shorter than W (function psd_argmax_fpk and its caller in src/mprsurge/analysis/ms11_eval.py). FACT, in words: A11 does not cut the record to the episode. It takes the spectrogram of the whole stored v of the run (Hann windows of length W, step as the window rule for the T_ramp, linear detrend, density scaling, time origin 0, window centres in seconds). From it it keeps the windows whose CENTRE lies inside [onset, end] of the classifier episode of the same seed at dt 1e-3 (the base run), inclusive with a tolerance of 1e-9 s, takes the mean PSD over those windows, and returns the frequency of the maximum of that mean in 25 <= f < 100 Hz, without interpolation. The same span (the base episode) is used for the other dt. If no window centre lies in the span the seed is NOT EVALUABLE ("no spectrogram window inside the episode window"). So an episode shorter than W is not a problem for A11: the window is not required to fit inside the episode, only its centre. Count: the base episodes at dt 1e-3, V_p 100, seeds 0, 1, 2 are 0.0833 s long each, against W = 0.3333 s and step 0.1667 s; all 3 of the 3 reading-(ii) comparisons (and so all 6 PSD evaluations) involve an episode shorter than W; no seed was NOT EVALUABLE, so a window centre fell in the span in all of them. The behaviour is NOT stated in the frozen rules (ms11_eval_rules.md section 3 says only 'argmax of the PSD of v in 25 to 100 Hz over the window of the classifier episode'): RULES GAP. The frozen rules file is not edited. CANDIDATE claim limit MS11-C8 (not entered as a limit until the reviewer rules): 'RB6 network reading (ii) f_pk for episodes shorter than W relies on a method not stated in the frozen rules (see the entry); the verdict stands as evaluated.' The independent script will implement this description (not a copy of the code); the row is marked 'method taken from original behaviour, arithmetic independent'. DL-400 is answered.

## DL-407  MS11 11g: the bounded post-hoc look at the RB9(b) map-1 cells; candidate claim limit MS11-C9    [ID: MS11, 11g, RB9, MS11-C9, DL-405, DL-406]
Date:            2026-10-27        Author:
Decision:        FACT, POST HOC, EXPLORATORY, read only, feeds no gate (scripts/ms11_9b_look.py, committed before the run, one run, exit 0; output results/A11/post_hoc_9b_look/ms11_9b_map1_estimator_look.csv and ms11_9b_map1_estimator_summary.json, git-ignored, labelled). 760 map-1 cells with an episode. Within 1/W (0.5 Hz): unwrapped Hilbert phase estimator 51 (equals A11), upward zero crossings 45 (equals the independent check). The two estimators disagree on 'within' in 18 cells: 12 are within by the Hilbert phase and outside by zero crossings, 6 the other way; 12 - 6 = 6 = 51 - 45, so the counts reconcile through the listed cells. No error, no cell-mapping problem (cell ids are the run stems; the 760 and the baseline classes were already equal). Nature of the 18 cells (table in the file): NOT near-bound flips as I had guessed in DL-405 (that hypothesis is withdrawn). In the 12 cells the zero-crossing frequency is 0.88 to 11.25 Hz away from the spectral f_pk (above it) while the Hilbert frequency is within 0.5 Hz of it; in the 6 cells the Hilbert frequency is 5.09 to 8.32 Hz below f_pk while the zero-crossing frequency is within 0.5 Hz. The largest difference between the two estimators over all 760 cells is 14.76 Hz. I did not investigate why (UNVERIFIED; possible waveform or amplitude-phase effects in the flagged episodes). Headline under both: spectral f_pk 49.0 Hz; Hilbert phase 44.609402 Hz (difference 4.390598 Hz); zero crossings 44.609421 Hz (difference 4.390579 Hz); bound 0.5 Hz: FAIL under either, difference 1.9e-5 Hz. The statement for MS11-C9 holds for the headline, so it is recorded. CANDIDATE claim limit MS11-C9 (not entered until the reviewer rules; worded as the prompt): 'the frozen rules do not name the estimator of the cycle frequency in RB9(b); the map-cell fractions are 51 of 760 (A11, Hilbert phase) and 45 of 760 (independent, zero crossings), both reported; the headline RB9(b) FAIL holds under either estimator'. Decision:        FACT and PROPOSAL (UNVERIFIED, not ruled). F4 is the next figure of M13-7 (b) after FS3 and F6 (DL-479 to DL-481); not ambiguous. F4 INPUTS (stored, all opened, readiness ready, scripts/ms13_inputs.py readiness): results/A7/a7_ramp_metrics.parquet (360 rows: S5 235 and S13 125; onsets under both readings, signed delays, the A4 prediction t_pred and delay_eta_pred, in_range, peak power, f_pk, duration; DL-180 to DL-186), results/A3/a3_sn_ramp.parquet (13 rows; DL-109, DL-110), results/A4/a4_rb3a_summary.json (headline cross-check, within 1e-6 of the A7 headline prediction: 1.7148841437563163 against 1.714884142549614 eta units, 115.22459921450229 against 115.22459917312965 s), results/A11/a11_robustness.csv (44 rows); and the JSON config (the ramp rate eps) of 373 run records: S5/ramp (105), S5/ramp_noise/p2_noise (130), S13 (125), A3/S2 (13). No .npz is opened and no series is drawn (M13-12). REGISTRY CHANGE (FOR THE REVIEWER): INPUTS["F4"] of scripts/ms13_inputs.py (13a: 9 entries) is replaced by these 4 files and 4 record families (counts 105, 130, 125, 13); the timing list is empty. Dropped from the 13a list, with the reason: the A2 ring map (see M2 RING SOURCE), the A4 range CSV (1,260 rows; the A7 table already holds the stored prediction and the in-range flag per run), the S5 baseline-only runs (1,226 records; they hold the noise baseline of G4, not an F4 quantity), the S11 (120) and S11_ctrl (30) records (the sigma-factor and control classes of S11 are FS3; the F4 noise band is the A7 family p2_noise, sigma 0.0624, 13 T_ramp x 10 seeds, mode N). ADDED to the registry: the A3 table and the A3/S2, S5/ramp_noise and S13 record families (they hold eps, which A7 does not). M2 RING SOURCE (decided from the stored files, M13-14 (v)): the A2 ring map (results/A2/a2_ring_map.npz) holds static arrays over (eta/Delta, J/sqrt(Delta)) (241 x 201 x 3: ring_is_focus, ring_in_G, ring_g1_nondamped, ring_r, Re and Im of lambda, growth and decay rate, ring frequency, cycles per e-fold) and the K4 fit; it has no ramp and is the FS1 input. The A3 table holds the 13 M2 ramps through the saddle-node (T_ramp 1 to 1000 s): jump time, eta at the jump, upper fold -3.136134, offset (0.34575 to 0.003430), the ring class (damped at 13 of 13) and the fitted ring rate (about -24 to -26 per s, SE 0.3 to 0.6, about 10 cycles) (DL-109, DL-110). F4 uses A3, because Table 8.1 lists A3 for F4 and F4 is a ramp-rate figure; A2 is not read. TABLE 8.1 RESULT "Onsets miss the A4 entry-exit prediction on the runs inside the RB3(a) range, or the floored delay (D43) depends on the Heun step (RB6) -> G6": first part OCCURRED: 0 of 6 testable in-range runs within one A4 step (match error 33.1, 20.6, 12.7, 7.6, 4.4 and 25.1 steps; 3 more in-range runs have eta constant at the predicted time), RB3(a) not judged at the headline (departure 3); G6 was ruled PASSED WITH DEPARTURES with claim limits G6-D1 to G6-D3 (DL-188, DL-208, DL-209). Second part DID NOT occur: the floored delay does not depend on the Heun step at the 1 ms output grid (the four rungs give identical values for all 30 seed pairs; DL-184, DL-190). Also RB6 solver clause FAIL (181 ms, DL-189), RB3(b) classifier onset FAIL and raw crossing PASS (DL-182, DL-186, DL-208), RB2 FAIL (DL-387). PANELS: (a) signed delay (raw first crossing primary, classifier onset secondary) against eps (log) for P1, P2, P5 x linear, sigmoid, 13 T_ramp, the A4 prediction as stored, a ring on in-range runs, the headline labelled RB6 FAIL; (b) to (e) peak power absolute and relative, f_pk, duration, with the mode-N noise band (min, max, median of 10 seeds); (f) P5 up delay, down offset, hysteresis width; (g) P1 start distance 0.5, 1.5, 3.0; (h) noise band on the delay; (i) and (j) the D43 floors at the headline under both onset readings; (k) and (l) the M2 ramp (A3): offset, ring rate and class. The quasi-static line: no quasi-static onset value is stored; the delay column is defined relative to eta_H, so the zero line is a reference by definition (UNVERIFIED reading) and nothing is recomputed. The A4 entry-exit prediction is drawn from the stored A7 column. D-none runs and the one run without a raw crossing are drawn at the axis foot. Readings applied from earlier rulings: DL-186 clarifications 1 (raw crossing primary), 2 (judge the testable in-range runs only), 3 (P1 start distance 0.5 has 5 in-range T_ramp), 5 and 6 (no pooled verdict), 7 (the Heun exact 0 is a limit of the 1 ms grid), 8 (floor delays are signed); clarification 4 (Radau) as G6-D2. G6-D1 TO G6-D3, WHERE: G6-D1 (no claim that onset follows the A4 prediction) appears in the caption and on the figure (the key row: inside the RB3(a) range judged, outside reported not judged; the status text: 0 of 6) because F4 draws the prediction next to the onsets; G6-D2 (headline delay from D43-floored runs; noise-free onset solver-dependent, DOP853 58.698 s, Radau 58.879 s) appears in the caption and on the figure (the headline point labelled RB6 FAIL; panels (i) and (j) draw the floored delays) because F4 draws both series separately; G6-D3 (RB3(b) under both onset readings) appears in the caption and on the figure (the double dagger is the classifier onset in (a); (i) raw crossing and (j) classifier onset side by side) because F4 draws onsets. REGISTRY CHANGE (FOR THE REVIEWER): INPUTS["F1"] of scripts/ms13_inputs.py loses the S8 mean-field companion (head60, T_ramp 60 s, not the headline) and the A8 sensitivity table (1,880 rows; F1 draws no A_ref-based series: the classifier threshold 0.1 x A_ref applies to the band-passed envelope, which F1 does not draw) and gains results/ms10/eval/ms10_eval.json and the A11 table; the S5 headline, S8 headline, A8 A_ref and criteria entries are kept. WHAT IS STORED: the 300-neuron raster is stored in every S8 network npz (raster_t_ms 1,777,037 spikes for seed 0 at 120 s, raster_neuron the neuron index, raster_j the 300 stored indices; 294 of the 300 spike); the binned rate is r (network: 1 ms bins; mean field: the solver output at 1 ms); the mean V is v; NO spectrogram is stored (no file under results/ holds one). SPECTROGRAM RULING APPLIED (DL-485 ruling 7): analysis.surge_metrics.spectrogram_v (the frozen routine, called without any change of frozen code) is applied to the stored v of the mean-field record and of network seed 0 with the settings of the frozen window rule (window_for_ramp(120 s): W = 2 s, step 1 s) and the frozen criteria (hann taper, primary band 25 to 100 Hz, total band 1 to 150 Hz); detrend linear and density scaling are those of the routine; sample i at i/fs (the classifier time origin; the stored network stamp is the bin end, 1 ms later). The caption states these settings; frequencies above 150 Hz are not drawn; power is shown as 10 log10 PSD, each panel on its own scale (the mean-field floor is about -400 dB; display choices, UNVERIFIED). DISPLAY DECIMATION (DL-485 ruling 6): each r(t) and v(t) series is drawn as a min-to-max envelope in 1300 blocks of whole samples; the extremes of every block and of the series are the stored extremes (tested); the mean field is a filled band, the network seeds are outlines (the fills of the three seeds merged in a trial render). Not decimated: eta(t) and J(t) (stored arrays), the raster (all stored spikes), the spectrograms. PANELS: (a) and (b) eta(t) and J(t) of the stored headline record with t_on, the end of the ramp, eta_start, eta_H and eta_peak from the stored path values (not retyped); (c) to (f) r(t) and v(t), mean field and the three network seeds at N = 1e4, same y range per quantity, the stored mean-field D-tr onset (58.698 s) as a line, the stored network classifier onset (S-sus, 12.0 s, all three seeds) and the three raw first crossings (50.924, 50.170, 50.857 s, post hoc, feed no gate) as marks; (g) and (h) spectrograms of v; (i) to (k) raster of seed 0, whole record and two 1 s windows that start at the stored network classifier onset (12.000 s) and at the stored mean-field onset (58.698 s). For every one of them the stored onset lies after t_on + T_ramp (the time the ramp reaches eta_peak; ramps.py: g(1) = 1 for the linear and the sigmoid profile, and P1 holds eta_peak after it): 6.050 > 6.0, 6.825 > 6.778, 6.198 > 6.0, 6.989 > 6.778, 6.105 > 6.0, 6.903 > 6.778, 8.304 > 8.162, 6.050 > 6.0 s. Conversely no P1 or P2 onset after t_on + T_ramp is below the maximum. P5 (path_updown) has no hold: its 8 onsets after t_on + T_ramp (T_ramp 1 and 1.778 s, both profiles, both readings) lie on the down leg and are below the maximum (1.818 to 1.953). The stored data agree with R8: no stop. ## DL-545  MS13 13t-1: rulings J1 to J15 of the journal export and the settings of configs/journal_export.yaml    [ID: MS13, 13t, 13t-1, DL-544, DL-511, DL-512]
Date:            2026-10-30        Author:
Decision:        RULED (reviewer, 13t-1 prompt; the full list is in docs/ms13_figure_rules.md, written in this step). J1 what stays on the image (panel letters in reading order, axis labels with units and symbols, legends, class legend marks, short titles with FAIL in every panel that shows a failed check, short in-panel lines that change how a panel reads, network symbols, "coincide" notes). J2 what moves out (DRAFT marks, "as ruled" footers, provenance text, status strips and blocks, G10 pointers, internal ID keys, long notes) to the caption or a supplement sheet per figure; no caption, figure number or title inside the figure file. J3 failures stay visible (every FAIL, NOT PASSED, NOT EVALUABLE or FAILED strip line in a panel title or the journal caption; the full strip in the supplement). J4 journal-neutral settings, ALL UNVERIFIED, ONE file configs/journal_export.yaml: double-column width at most 7.5 in; single-column width 84 mm as a second setting (the sources disagree whether 84 or 174 mm is the single column); height at most 8.75 in; all text at least 8 pt at the final size (the draft tick-label rule stays for the drafts); Arial or Helvetica if installed, else DejaVu Sans (and said so); vector text and lines; fonts embedded as real fonts (pdf.fonttype 42, ps.fonttype 42, no Type 3); line width at least 0.3 pt; RGB; PNG 300 dpi, a 600 dpi TIFF (flattened, LZW, no alpha) and an EPS only if they build without error; the vector PDF is the main output. J5 the export is mode="journal" of the existing make_<ID> code, so the drawn-data digest equals the draft's; outputs figures/journal/<ID>/ and figures/journal/supplement/; scripts/fig_journal.py <ID> reads only results/. J6 the journal caption is the draft caption rebuilt with the same builder, same stored numbers; the independent comparison applies. J7 pilot F1, F3, F5 only. J8 no collisions (checked by code and by eye; allow-list entries need a stated reason, are logged and go to the user for approval). J9 layout is not data. J10 the F1 draft faults to remove. J11 docs/ms13_figure_rules.md. J12 the F2 (13t-2) and F3 (13t-1) draft faults to remove. J13 colour and accessibility (magma, viridis, cividis only; colour bars with units; non-colour distinction; greyscale and colour-vision simulation with an installed package, otherwise STOP that item; lightness difference as the measure, threshold UNVERIFIED; text contrast 4.5:1). J14 file names, rasterized heavy artists, sizes, export_manifest.csv, nothing uploaded. J15 how to work (verification script, checklist and progress files, independent subagent review, no weakened check). VALUES CHOSEN IN configs/journal_export.yaml (all UNVERIFIED, none claims a journal requirement): double_column_width_in 7.5; single_column_width_mm 84; max_height_in 8.75; text min_pt 8, title_pt 8; font_preferred Arial, Helvetica, fallback DejaVu Sans; pdf_fonttype 42, ps_fonttype 42; lines min_width_pt 0.3; colour allowed_cmaps magma, viridis, cividis, forbidden jet, rainbow, hsv, turbo, gist_rainbow, nipy_spectral, gist_ncar; min_text_contrast 4.5; min_lightness_difference 15 (CIELAB L*; the threshold of the greyscale report); output dpi 300, tiff_dpi 600, pdf_size_flag_mb 5; collision pad_pt 0.5; file-name pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_+=,.-]+$. matplotlib has no per-artist dpi: rasterized artists use the savefig dpi (said in the config comment). READINGS MADE HERE (UNVERIFIED, for the reviewer): (a) "all text at least 8 pt" is read as the font size of every drawn glyph run, so the export writes no mathtext subscript (matplotlib draws sub- and superscripts at 0.7 of the text size); tau_d is written with the Greek letter, an underscore and d, eta-bar as a mathtext bar over the Greek letter (no subscript). (b) The PDF check B uses no PDF-reading package (none is installed: only matplotlib, numpy, pandas, pillow, fonttools and scipy are); the text overlaps are taken from the matplotlib renderer and the PDF file itself is checked by reading its objects (font subtype, embedded font file, no Type 3, the font-size operators, the page box). (c) No installed package simulates colour-vision deficiency (deuteranopia, protanopia, tritanopia); that part of J13 is STOPPED and reported; the greyscale lightness check uses pillow. style.py already holds UNVERIFIED hand-written matrices for two deficiencies (13c, written from memory); they are NOT used for the export without the reviewer's ruling.

(2) HOW THE DRAWING WAS DONE (a departure from the wording of J5, for the reviewer): the journal mode shares load_<ID>, prepare_<ID> (so the drawn-data digest is the draft's), the mark helpers, the caption builder and the notes with the draft, but it has its own layout function per figure inside the same module (_draw_F1_journal, _draw_F3_journal, _draw_F5_journal); a single drawing function with a mode switch on every line would have changed the draft code path. F1 and F5 place their axes in inches (no layout engine): constrained layout collapsed the axes on F5 at 8.7 in. (3) THE VERIFIER CAUGHT FIVE REAL FAULTS IN THE FIRST JOURNAL RENDERS, all fixed before the recorded build: (a) F5 (i) log axis printed 10^3 to 10^5 with mathtext exponents drawn at 5.6 pt (0.7 of 8 pt): the tick labels are now plain 1e3, 1e4, 1e5 (G9 number format); (b) the F1 mean-field onset line (D-tr colour, dashed) and the dashed seed 1 envelope, and the dashed band edges, differed in colour only: the onset line is dash-dotted in the journal export (F1J_ONSET_LS; the style table's D-tr line style is unchanged); (c) the three F1 raw first-crossing marks were one shape in three shades: in the journal export they use the seed marks of the style table (circle, plus, star; SERIES_MARK_KEYS), and the key says so; (d) F3 P4a and P4b in (d) were both dashed once their start marks are not drawn: P4b is dotted in the journal export (F3_PATH_LS_J); (e) F5 (b) put the network-disagree red (#d73027) and the D-none green (#1b7837) in one axes at nearly the same lightness (L* 47 and 43): the journal export fills the disagree symbol with #fb6a4a (F5J_COLOURS). All are layout or style, no drawn value. The audit rule of the 13o and 13p tests (no literal colour, marker, point size or font size in drawing code) flagged literals in the journal drawing code (white mark faces, 4.0 pt sizes, one grey); they are now style.py constants (F3_COMBINED small_size, F5J_COLOURS separator), no test changed. The F5 (b) title reads 'RB1 cells FAIL' (as the draft) and the F3 caption sentence names the line styles of P4a (dashed) and P4b (dotted). (4) WHAT THE CHECKER DOES AND DOES NOT DO: pad 0.5 pt (config); a filled FancyBboxPatch is a container (text must lie wholly in it); an Annotation is drawn unclipped (annotation_clip), so clipped-text is tested for plain texts only; marker extents come from the marker path (a tall narrow bar is narrow); rasterized artists count as images for text and as non-markers for marker-marker; collections other than scatter are tested through their data extent; line crossings of lines with lines are not tested (J8 lists text, markers, legends, images, frames and the figure edge). (5) THE ALLOW-LIST (collide.JOURNAL_ALLOW; each entry needs the reviewer's approval): F3 panel (a) and (b) marker-marker 'slice Hopf points' with '25 Hz crossings' (stored positions: the Hopf point and the 25 Hz crossing of one slice, eta_bar 1.161 and 1.261 at tau_d 3 ms in (a), 1.439 and 1.629 at 5 ms in (b), are closer than the two marks are wide; not moved); F3 panel (c) marker-marker 'slice Hopf points' with the A6 headline Hopf point (the Hopf point of the 5 ms slice of the Delta 0.3 panel is the headline Hopf point, eta_bar 2.896, one stored point drawn twice, a tri-up inside a ring); F1 panels (d) and (f) marker-marker among the three raw first-crossing marks (the stored times 50.170, 50.857 and 50.924 s lie within about 0.01 in at the panel scale; G7: stored positions are kept and the key says the three seeds coincide). (6) NOT DONE, for the reviewer: colour-vision-deficiency simulation (no installed package; STOP, nothing home-made); text boxes from the PDF (no installed PDF reader; the text overlaps come from the matplotlib renderer, the PDF is checked as bytes); the F1 and F3 and F5 PNG crops are looked at in the recorded build (DL-548). ## DL-554  MS13 13t-1b: rulings R1 to R10 (venue Peer Community Journal, colour-vision simulation, allow-list, FAIL placement, wording of "coincide", edge slivers, F5 cell marks, process, source-data size)    [ID: MS13, 13t, 13t-1b, DL-545, DL-547, DL-550, DL-551, DL-553]
Date:            2026-10-31        Author:
Decision:        RULED (reviewer, 13t-1b prompt; the full text is in docs/ms13_figure_rules.md, section R1 to R10). R1 VENUE (supersedes the conflicting parts of J4, J5, J9 and J14): the target is Peer Community Journal (PCJ) after a Peer Community In recommendation; PCJ prefers jpg, tiff or png figures, forbids svg, wmf and emf, states no resolution, size or colour rule and places figures in line with the text inside 2.54 cm margins. MAIN files: PNG 600 dpi and flattened TIFF (LZW, no alpha) 600 dpi (UNVERIFIED defaults); the vector PDF is an extra (300 dpi for rasterized parts); never SVG, WMF or EMF; EPS only as an extra if it builds without error. MAIN width 6.3 in (UNVERIFIED: the PCJ template and page size were not read; A4 minus two 2.54 cm margins is 15.9 cm = 6.26 in), maximum height 8.0 in so that a caption fits on the page (UNVERIFIED); a second setting up to 7.5 in stays for other journals. Text at least 8 pt at the final physical size, fonts embedded, no Type 3. File names <ID>_journal.png and <ID>_journal.tiff (main), <ID>_journal.pdf (extra). A PDF above 5 MB and a PNG or TIFF above 10 MB are flagged. The checks run on the main PNG and TIFF and on the PDF text boxes with the new config values. R2: no colour-vision simulation in code (no package installed, none to be installed); the greyscale L* check and the non-colour-attribute check stay; the verifier row "cvd" reads "MANUAL (user checks final PNGs with an online simulator; UNVERIFIED)" and does not make the verifier exit non-zero; the hand-written matrices in style.py are not used. R3: the allow-list is approved with conditions: F3 (a)/(b) Hopf mark against the 25 Hz bar (stored positions); F3 (c) the A6 headline Hopf point is the 5 ms slice's Hopf point (one stored point drawn twice; the caption says so); F1 (d) and (f) the three raw first-crossing marks overlap at the figure scale (wording per R6). R4: F5 (a) shows the RB1 cells result and F5 (g) draws network f_pk, so both titles carry FAIL (red title as defined for F5); the RB2 1.0_sigma FAIL is drawn in no F5 panel and stays in the caption and the supplement (J3); the F1 status-strip membership is NOT changed (settled by DL-488 and later); one sentence is added to the F1 caption: "Other failed checks on the headline path (RB6 solver onset 181 ms against 1 ms; RB2 headline class 7 of 10 seeds at the noise level used; RB3(b) classifier onset) are shown in F4 and FS4." with the values taken from the stored A11 table (a value that is not stored is left out). R5 accepted as reported: tau_d with an underscore (no mathtext subscripts below 8 pt); F1 and F5 use their own layout code in figures.py (DL-547 (2)) with the equality of the drawn-data digest to the draft as the control; the rewrite of the two shared manifest rows (figures.py, style.py) as in DL-541 and DL-551. R6 WORDING OF "COINCIDE" IN F1: the draft label reads "raw crossings: 3 seeds coincide" but the stored raw first crossings are 50.170, 50.924 and 50.857 s (seed order 0, 1, 2: 50.924, 50.170, 50.857; span 0.754 s); only the three classifier onsets (12.000 s) are equal. Ruled: the stop rule does NOT stop this step for it; the drafts are left unchanged; the wording is fixed only in the journal text ("overlap at this scale: stored values 50.170 to 50.924 s"), the alt text and the caption; a close item (item 40 of docs/ms13_close_items.md) says that the draft label needs the same correction at the next draft rebuild; the word "coincide" is used only where stored values are equal. R7: the thin white bands at the left and right edges of F1 (g) and (h) are stated in one caption sentence from the stored window length and step (W 2 s, step 1 s) and the stored time vector; where no window is stored the cells are blank; if the stored times do not settle it the text is "blank in the stored record; cause not determined (UNVERIFIED)". R8: the in-cell glyphs of F5 (c) and (d) (about 0.03 in tall) are replaced by a mark or hatch pattern that is distinguishable at the cell size and appears in the key exactly as plotted, the non-colour check keeps passing; if it cannot be done within two attempts that item stops and the problem is described. R9: if a safety check blocks a command, report it and do not reword the command to get past it (the ${SP:?} rewrite for deleting own scratch files in 13t-1 is accepted this once). R10: the source-data CSV of F1 (28 MB) is kept; the supplement notes that it is to be zipped for the Zenodo record. FILES CHANGED IN THIS COMMIT: docs/ms13_figure_rules.md (R1 to R10 section, markers on J4, J5, J9, J14), docs/ms13_export_checklist.json (every F1, F3, F5 item reset to failing because the layout is redone at 6.3 x 8.0 in; new items for R1, R2, R4, R6, R7, R8, R10), docs/ms13_13t_progress.md, docs/ms13_close_items.md (item 40). READINGS (UNVERIFIED, for the reviewer): (a) "6.3 in" is the MAIN width and "8.0 in" the maximum height; the 7.5 x 8.75 in setting is kept in the config as the second setting and is not used by the pilot; (b) the sentence of R4 is used verbatim; the stored A11 table gives RB6 solver_onset_headline value 181 ms, threshold 1 ms (FAIL), RB2 headline_class_kept_1.0_sigma value 7 of 10, threshold >= 8 of 10 (FAIL), and RB3 b_classifier_onset (FAIL, no value stored, so no number is written for it); the draft captions show RB2 7 of 10 in F4 (also F5 and FS3), not in FS4, and RB6 solver and RB3(b) in F4 and FS4, so F4 and FS4 together hold all three; (c) the PNG at 600 dpi is the main file, the figure is created at the PDF dpi (300) and saved to the PNG and TIFF at 600 dpi, so the collision checker (pixels at the figure dpi) is unchanged in its meaning.

The plan states three things about figure captions: (1) section 8 Conventions [R5, SQ3]: 'full parameters and spectrogram settings in each caption.' (2) Section 8: 'Each figure also gets a Nordlie parameter table [R5, SQ6; R7, section 2.5] [verified].' (3) Manuscript and submission checklist (MS15, below Table 11.2): 'Nordlie parameter tables, one per experiment or figure; every caption states the parameter regime and the take-home message [R7, section 8(d)].' Section 7.2 and Table 7.2 say nothing about captions; Table 11.1 (MS13: 'Figures F1-FS6 with provenance', gate 'Each built from a clean tree and tagged') says nothing about captions.
