## DL-593  MS13 13t-1f: rulings V5 to V8 (stranger-readable SHORT captions, fixes by figure, failed checks, word limits)    [ID: MS13, 13t, 13t-1f, V5, V6, V7, V8, F1, F3, F5, F5c]
Date:            2026-11-04        Author:
Decision:        RULED by the reviewer (13t-1f prompt), logged before any trial render. V5 RULE: every technical term used in a SHORT caption is defined in that caption, in plain words, in one clause, where it is first used, or is an ordinary English word. Terms to define when used: surge (a transient rise of gamma-band power, 25 to 100 Hz); the classes (S+: the power rises in absolute and relative terms and ends; S-rel: relative rise only; S-abs: absolute rise only; S-sus: a rise that does not end; NS: none; D-tr, D-sus, D-none: the same three outcomes for the noise-free mean field: an episode that ends, one that does not end, none); mean field (the model's equations for the average activity of the population, noise-free unless said) and network (the simulated network of N spiking neurons); main example (the run fixed before the analysis as the main case); the hypoxia-like path P2 (mean excitability raised and coupling J ramped to 0 after a delay); P1 to P5 only if mentioned, one clause each as in the full-caption Key; Hopf point (where the resting state starts to oscillate); cycle frequency (frequency of that oscillation) and spectral peak (the peak of the power spectrum of the simulated signal); slice (one fixed tau_d); map cell, noisy subgrid, ramp seed (a simulated network run with the ramp, one per random seed) and control (the same network without the ramp); onset and duration (when the classifier first and last flags the gamma rise); first crossing (when the signal first crosses the classifier threshold, UNVERIFIED if the plan does not say; then 'first crossing of its detection threshold' only). Every definition is taken from the plan or the full-caption Key; a term with neither is written as it stands and listed UNVERIFIED in the report; nothing is invented. V6 FIXES BY FIGURE (review: docs/ms13_13t1e_review.md; full captions change only where a number or statement was wrong). F1: sentence 2 states that by eye the network envelopes in (d) and (f) look similar to the mean-field ones in (c) and (e) and that the failed check concerns the class given by the fixed classifier, which labels all three network runs S-sus (no end); 'no claim is made about the visual shape, either way' stays; the three seeds nearly coincide at this scale; (d) and (f) use the same y axes as (c) and (e); the dashed horizontal lines in (g) and (h) are 25 and 100 Hz (the gamma band); the orange frames in (i) are the two windows of (j) and (k); the units or meaning of J (negative = inhibitory); 49.0 Hz is the peak of the power spectrum of the mean-field run and is not drawn (said so). F3: point counts out of the SHORT caption ('drawn as straight segments between recorded points'; the full caption keeps 30 and 100); a 25 Hz bar is absent at slices where the cycle never crosses 25 Hz (7, 6 and 3 of 9 slices have one, as recorded); the grey open circle in (c) and (d) is the start of the paths (eta_bar 1.396) and the dark ring is the Hopf point of the main example at tau_d 5 ms; P1, P2, P3 and P5 are drawn as one arrow because their eta_bar, Delta and tau_d are equal, P4a and P4b separately; 'values from the project log' becomes 'values from the analysis record listed in the supplement'. F5: sentence 1 becomes 'The surge result holds for the noise-free mean field only: the network disagrees with it at 3 of the 4 cells tested, and the noisy mean field agrees with the noise-free map in 97 of 225 cells (43.1 percent; 203 cells, 90 percent, were needed)'; how a network cell agrees stated in plain words (all 3 seeds in a surge class S+, S-rel or S-abs when the mean field is D-tr; the plan's rule, wording copied from the full caption) so that cell 1 reads as agreeing; cells numbered 1 to 4 in (a) and (b); map 1 is 30 x 30 in (Delta, tau_d) at ramp duration 120 s and map 2 is in (J0, T_ramp); the network cells and their matching mean-field run use T_ramp 30 s while the map is at 120 s, no equivalence claimed; what a tie is (an equal split, counted as a disagreement by the rule); (d) is the same cells re-scored by a rule chosen after the results (post hoc) and feeds no check; the dashed frame of (d) marks it as post hoc. F5c: define surge class (S+, S-rel, S-abs) and write the S-sus counts separately, from the figure arrays: controls in a surge class 0, 2, 1, 1 of 3 and controls in S-sus 0, 0, 2, 2 of 3 at N = 1000, 3000, 10,000, 30,000 (both checked against the arrays; a difference is a STOP); the Limits sentence '10 of 10 ... 10 of 10' gets its scope in plain words as in the full caption (other runs, not the controls drawn here) and says that one ramp seed at N = 10,000 is NS and that the drawn ramp seeds are not 10 of 10 in a surge class; the dotted line in (b) and (c) is the matching mean-field run and the dashed line in (d) is the smallest duration the classifier can give (one window, 1000 ms); what peak frequency, onset and duration refer to (V5). V7 FAILED CHECKS IN THE SHORT CAPTION: list only the failed checks whose result is drawn in the figure or bound to a drawn quantity (F1: network against mean field, the main example and the cells; F3: the frequency check; F5: network against mean field at the cells, the 90 percent agreement rule; F5c: the step-halving check), each in one plain clause with its number where short and explained in plain words (what the check tests, in one clause), then one sentence 'N further failed checks of the project are not shown in this figure; all are listed in Supplement <ID>', N being the number of other failed rows in the full-caption list of that figure (computed by a test from the full caption; they must agree). The full caption lists every one, unchanged. The sentence 'All earlier failures and limits stand ...' stays, with '(listed in the supplement)'. V8 WORD LIMITS: F1 400, F3 330, F5 330, F5c 330 (UNVERIFIED, configs/journal_export.yaml). (1) C9: journal.sentence_case(fig) runs in J.finish of every journal figure: the first letter of every label that starts with a lower-case word is capitalised (after a panel prefix '(a) '), also the tick labels (their formatter is wrapped); exceptions as ruled (eta_bar, Delta, J, tau_d, tau, T_ramp, t_on, N, f, the class names, M3, ING, P1 to P5, panel letters, units, FAIL, FAILED) plus, read as ruled symbols and not as words, the failure-label keys 'a' to 'h' (plan failure labels a to h) and the variable letters r, v, s, t of 'r, v, s: ...'; labels left in lower case: only these. The F1 schematic words are written in sentence case at the source (journal-only constant F1J_SCHEMATIC: 'N: network size', 'spike raster', 'rate, mean potential, synapse'); the drafts are not touched. Words with a capital inside a label are the proper nouns Hopf and Lorentzian and the symbol Delta (reported by journal.capitals_inside, not a failure). The new verifier row 'sentence case' fails on any other label. (2) C1: F2 (c) has the red title '(c) Network vs mean field: FAIL' and the one note 'The network and mean-field classes disagree elsewhere (check failed); this panel compares amplitudes only' (red, upper left, placed at the first attempt without touching); the old 'not drawn at and below the Hopf point' line moved to the lower left in two lines; the y label of (c) names the v amplitude. TITLE_MAP gets the F2 row (RB1) and the plain titles of F2 and F6 are written as drawn (capital first letter). Because the red title is the four RB1 rows, JS.SHORT_NAMED['F2'] now holds the four RB1 rows (they are named in the red-title sentence of the short caption) and the short caption of F2 ends with 'No other failed check is about this figure' (it said '4 further failed checks'); the full caption names the rows as before. This follows from C1 (a red title needs the failed check it shows). (3) C2: the stable fixed point is drawn and keyed with the explicit dash-dot pattern (2.0, 1.0, 0.5, 1.0) x line width (period 9.9 pt at 2.2 pt) and the key handle is 3.7 font sizes = 29.6 pt (3.0 periods). The key still fits at 6.3 in. (4) C3: STOP on sentence 1 of the F2 short caption: the RULED take-home F2_TAKE_HOME (draft, DL-128, DL-129) reads 'The N = 1e4 network sweep does not follow the mean-field branch closely: its v amplitude differs from the mean field by +13.2 to -2.5 percent above eta_bar 3.0 ... below the Hopf point it does not rest (v amplitude 0.22 to 0.31) ...'. The drawn numbers: the 18 plotted network steps above eta_bar 2.996 lie between -0.0248 and +0.1317 relative to the mean field; in (a) and (b) the network symbols lie on the mean-field branch to the eye (the relative differences are 13.2 (up sweep) and 12.4 (down sweep) percent at eta_bar 3.296, about 7 percent at 3.696 and at most 4.8 percent from 4.096 up; -2.5 percent at 6.496). My reading: the ruled words 'does not follow ... closely' conflict with what (a) and (b) show; the ruled text is NOT changed, sentence 1 of the short and the full caption is the ruled text as before, and the reviewer is asked for the replacement sentence (proposal: 'Above the Hopf point the network amplitude lies close to the mean-field branch in (a) and (b) and differs from it by up to 13.2 percent in (c)'). The other parts of C3 are done: the sweep is defined in plain words ('in a sweep eta_bar is raised step by step, then lowered again'); two facts read from the arrays: the largest difference between the network up and down sweeps in the v amplitude is 0.095 (1.071 up, 1.166 down) at eta_bar 2.896, above eta_bar 3.0 it is 0.080 at eta_bar 5.696; at the Hopf point the network v amplitude is 1.07 (up sweep) and 1.17 (down sweep) against 0.08 and 0.55 for the mean field (the mean-field values are the up and down steps at the Hopf eta_bar 2.896; the steps within 0.1 of it are still relaxing, as the figure says) and below the Hopf point the network does not rest (0.22 to 0.31); the two limit sentences are one ('stated for model M3 only and stated for the mean field only (not for the network), and there is no claim that it is robust to finite-size fluctuations'); the sentence 'no classifier or spectrogram is used' is not in the short caption (the full caption keeps it). (5) C4: F6 short caption: every item (a) to (g) of C4 is in; the counts read from the arrays are 24 points = 20 pre-registered runs and 4 P2 comparator runs (STOP condition not met); the identical peak frequencies are 48.048, 49, 49 and 49.5 Hz for P3 (drive 0.5 and 1), P4b and the P2 comparators (STOP condition not met; the build raises an error if they differ); map 2 any-label bars are dotted ('...'), map 1 hatched ('//'); negative control 2 is D-tr at 13 of 13 ramp durations with the drive off and 13 of 13 on; the plan (section 2.4) gives NC2 as 'the full path with I(t) = 0 versus I(t) on' and NC3 as 'inhibition raised while eta_bar falls' (exploratory), written in plain words; the ruled sigma limit G4-C4 is added to the journal captions of F6 only (SHORT_LIMIT_IDS and the limits paragraph of the journal caption; the draft claim list F6_CLAIM_LIMITS is not changed, the draft is byte-identical). (6) C5: F5, F5c, F3, F1 clauses in as ruled (numbers read from the arrays: 173 of 225 = 76.9 percent; the arrays hold no S-rel seed (40 ramp seeds and 12 controls); 3 controls per N; control onsets 10.0 to 33.0 s); the F3 question 'why do the bands end before eta_bar 8 in (a) and (b)' is NOT answered by the stored data (the stored A6 summary has branch_end_eta 4.70, 4.60, 4.86, 5.56 and 6.78 for the slices tau_d 1 to 8 ms at Delta 0.05, and 8.0 for the others, status ok, but no stop reason): listed as open in docs/ms13_13t3_notes.md. (8) C7: the verifier prints the allow-list by reason class with counts and fails for F2, F6 and the FS figures when a listed hit has a reason that is not a stored coincidence, a ruled size or a value on a reference line. Date:            2026-11-06        Author:
Decision:        FACT. (1) The review (docs/ms13_13t3_review.md, word for word; 36 files opened: the six short captions and 30 images) counts items 1 / 2 / 3 per figure: F1 14/4/18, F2 10/5/8, F3 12/3/15, F5 15/0/17, F5c 13/0/10, F6 16/4/29. No rebuild after the review (W6); every finding below is left for the reviewer. (2) TRIAGE. Real caption fault: F6 sentence (a) says the failure labels are 'listed in the key above panel (a)' but the key stands BELOW the bars of (a) (C4 a wording was 'above'; the ruling's own wording was followed): to be changed to 'below' in the next round. F2 sentence 1: the reviewer independently finds that 'does not follow the mean-field branch closely' contradicts (a) and (b): this is the STOP of DL-630, ruled text unchanged; the reviewer also notes that the Hopf-point values 0.08 and 0.55 and the 2.996 limit are not readable on the image (they are recorded numbers, stated as such) and that the network has 15 steps against the 61 of the mean field (the caption says '15 for the network'). F1: the classifier onset 12.0 s precedes any visible rise in (d) and (f) (close item 44, unchanged; the caption already says the network classes are a classifier result and that no claim is made about the visual shape); 'envelope', '(j) and (k)' content and 'detection threshold' undefined (open, not ruled). F3: the logic of 'the paths coincide in (c) and (d) because they differ in J, drive or time course' reads as confusing: it is the wording ruled in C5; left. F5: nothing contradicted; (e) has no result sentence in the caption (open). F5c: nothing contradicted. F6: the (d), (e) axes label the 120 s data point at the tick 100 (log ticks 10, 30, 100, 300 are the image's ticks; the data are at 10, 30, 120, 300 s), P3 drive 2 and P4a are plotted and not mentioned in the sentence on equal values, 'the same amount' and 'exploratory' are not explained: left. Terms the reviewers could not follow are the ones already listed UNVERIFIED in jf26.UNDEFINED_UNVERIFIED plus those of the review; nothing new is defined. (3) C9 labels left in lower case, with the reason: continuation lines of multi-line labels (the second line of a two-line title such as 'frequency check: FAIL' under '(a) Delta = 0.05', the wrapped lines of the F1 schematic and of two-line axis labels, the second line of the F6 row labels): the rule is applied to the start of each label (text object), not to a line break inside it; the failure-label descriptions of the F6 key start with their key letter ('b: tau_d outside window'); the key letters a to h, the variable letters r, v, s, t and the symbols are exceptions. The reviewer lists these lines as lower-case starts. (4) The final fast suite found three older tests that pin the lower-case text of an image label; their expected text is compared in lower case (no data assertion changes): tests/test_ms13_13t.py test_s9_and_s13 (power spectral), test_s11_s12 (colour-bar label, F5 (d) and F3 (e) titles), test_t6 (colour-bar label, 'ramp start and end' key text). ## DL-646  MS13 13t-5 G2 (b): READ-ONLY check of the FS1 test-point colour in (c) against the ringing in (d): the two DISAGREE in value; item STOPPED, nothing patched    [ID: MS13, 13t, 13t-5, G2, FS1, DL-642]
Date:            2026-11-07        Author:
Decision:        FACT (read-only; stored arrays of results/A2 (ring map) and results/S1 (K4 record) through prepare_FS1; nothing was drawn or changed). TABLE. (c) draws at the test point (eta_bar/Delta -5, J/sqrt(Delta) 15; grid node eta index 100, J index 150): a stable-focus node (the third root slot; the node has three fixed points), focus rate r = 1.0306, frequency 52.82 Hz (inside the 25 to 100 Hz band, class: in band, drawn), decay rate 0.3089, cycles per e-fold 1.710 (dark end of the cividis scale; the neighbouring nodes give 1.56 to 1.85); the node is not on the grey boundary in the stored arrays (it is a drawn, in-band node). (d) draws the recorded step response to the input step to I = 3: ringing YES (253 local maxima of r(t) at the 11 ms spacing of the record, falling from 2.867 at 28 ms to 1.373 at 2791 ms; r settles on the focus value r* 1.37324); the linearisation of the stored K4 row at the post-step fixed point gives lambda = -0.2318 + 5.7664 i per tau (tau 10 ms), i.e. 91.77 Hz and 5.766/(2 pi x 0.2318) = 3.96 cycles per e-fold. The two figures differ (52.8 Hz and 1.71 cycles per e-fold in (c); 91.8 Hz and 3.96 in (d)). MY READING (from the stored fields only): the focus of (c) (r = 1.0306) and the focus of (d) (r* = 1.3732, 'post-step fixed point') are not the same fixed point: (d) is the response to a step of the input current to 3.0 and settles on the focus of the stepped system, while the map (c) is read here as the ring map of the unstepped node; the stored record does not state the input current of the map, so this is a reading and not verified (UNVERIFIED). The reviewer's perception (about 1 cycle per e-fold or less in (c)) is consistent with the stored 1.71 at the dark end of the scale; the ringing in (d) is real. By the ruling the item is STOPPED and nothing is patched: no caption or image change is made for it; for the reviewer: whether the caption should say that (d) is the response after the step to I = 3.0 whereas (b) and (c) are read at the node as stored.

The FS figures go to the supplement of the paper and the Zenodo record as separate files, so they keep their own size: width and height of the draft (7.4 in wide; 11.2 to 14.4 in tall; UNVERIFIED limits 7.4 x 14.4 in, per figure in configs/journal_export.yaml fs_profile), no squeezing, NO split, NO relayout unless a check fails. A check that fails because of the draft layout (text below 8 pt, touching marks or labels) is fixed with the smallest layout change (font size, spacing, a shorter label), at most two attempts per overlap; if that fails, STOP that figure and propose a split (the pre-approval of Z2 stays valid for that case and its conditions: no panel dropped, array union and digests equal the draft's, own captions, mapping table, logged as a departure). This replaces Z1 (6.3 in wide, up to 9.5 in tall) for the FS figures FS2 to FS5; FS1 stays as built. H2 FS CAPTIONS. ONE caption per FS figure (not a short and a full one), no word limit, file <ID>_journal_caption.txt, in the seven labelled paragraphs of 13t-1d (take-home with the main failure in plain words; one sentence per panel; key and abbreviations containing only the terms used; classifier and spectrogram settings; parameters; failed checks, every one that concerns the figure, with what it tests; limits, every ruled claim limit with the same meaning and numbers), plain words, every term defined where first used, scope statements where a count refers to runs that are not drawn, no plan, milestone, DL or step reference, no code or key names (those go to the supplement tables). The supplement still carries the table 'plain title -> check ID', the stored key names, the parameter list, the source-data CSV and the alt text. FS1 keeps its short caption as built; no further caption work on FS1 except H5.

Date:            2026-11-09        Author:
Decision:        CHANGE (planned, logged before the edit). (1) LIMIT: configs/journal_export.yaml caption.short_max_words_FS1 600 -> 650 (UNVERIFIED, owner ruling X1, DL-716); the one place where it is defined; the FS1 assertions of tests/test_ms13_13t4.py (test_fs1_captions_numbers_and_main_failures: len(short.split()) <= 600) change to 650 (test text edit, no data assertion changes). (2) WORDING (src/mprsurge/plotting/jfs.py): new function fs1_testpoint(a2, d, c) reads from results/A2/a2_ring_map.npz at build time (never typed): the test-point node (eta/Delta = k_eta/k_Delta, J/sqrt(Delta) = k_J/sqrt(k_Delta), found by exact coordinates), its single stable-focus slot (ring_is_focus), ring_r, ring_freq_hz and ring_cycles_per_efold there (panel (c) values at input I = 0), and from k4_lambda and tau_ms the post-step values (frequency = Im(lambda)/(2 pi tau), cycles per e-fold = Im(lambda)/(2 pi |Re(lambda)|)), with k4_r_star; it stops with a named error if the node is not a single focus, if the input current of the root-count record is not the starting input of the S1 record, if Im(k4_lambda) differs from k4_omega_lin, or if the post-step fixed point differs from k4_r_star. The (c) sentence gets: 'At the circled test point, read with the input current at 0, the stable focus has ...'; the (d) sentence gets: 'After the step to 3 the system settles on a different stable focus (firing rate against firing rate at input 0); its oscillation, computed from the equations near that focus, has ... Hz and ... cycles per e-fold, so the values of (c) at the test point do not describe this ringing.' in the full and the short caption; frequencies with 2 decimals (as the existing 52.82 style) and cycles per e-fold with 2 decimals (the format of the existing 'largest 5.10'), so the notes' 1.710 reads 1.71 and 3.96 reads 3.96 (reported); firing rates with 4 decimals as in the caption. D3 READING (what sets `draft`, quoted from the code): (1) src/mprsurge/plotting/figprov.py line 169 and 170: `if tag_build and dirty: raise DirtyTreeError("a tagged build needs a clean tree (git status --porcelain is not empty)")`, where `dirty = bool(dirty_lines(root))` (line 168; `git status --porcelain`, so modified and untracked files count, git-ignored results/ and figures/ do not); line 177: `"draft": dirty or not tag_build`. So draft is false only if tag_build is True AND the tree is clean, and tag_build=True on a dirty tree raises before anything is written: a dirty tree can never record draft = false (this already holds in figprov and is not changed). The docstring (line 152) says "tag_build=True refuses a dirty tree; draft = dirty or untagged". (2) tag_build is meant to be set by the --tag option of the eleven draft scripts scripts/fig_F1.py to scripts/fig_FS5.py: `ap.add_argument("--tag", action="store_true", help="tagged build: refuse a dirty tree (no tag is created)")`, then `subprocess.run([sys.executable, scripts/check_clean_tree.py])` first (a non-zero code is returned at once) and `figures.make_<ID>(tag_build=a.tag)`; "a tag itself is never created here" (the docstrings). docs/ms13_conventions.md line 56: "A build without `--tag` may run on a dirty tree and is marked `draft`; a tagged build refuses a dirty tree." (3) scripts/fig_journal.py has no --tag and calls `getattr(figures, f"make_{fid}")(mode="journal", root=root)`, so tag_build keeps its default False and every journal record says draft = true even on a clean tree. (4) Every journal builder already carries tag_build to write_figure_provenance: make_F1, make_F3, make_F5 (prov_kw), _make_F2_journal, _make_F6_journal, _make_FS1_journal, jf4.build (via make_F4, argument tag_build), jfs2.build, jfs3.build, jfs4.build, jfs5.build (argument tag_build) all pass `tag_build=tag_build` (read at figures.py lines 1457, 5838, 6740, 7167, 7290, 2212 and jf4.py 592, jfs2.py 328, jfs3.py 291, jfs4.py 399, jfs5.py 442). In journal mode every drawing call has `draft=False` fixed (figures.py lines 935, 939, 942, 964, 972, 1430, 5812, 6759, 7154, 7275), so the image does not depend on tag_build. (5) TWO fixed texts in the journal supplement that do not follow the flag: src/mprsurge/plotting/journal.py line 321, the first line of every <ID>_supplement.md, `# {fig_id} supplement sheet (journal export; draft = true)` (the word true is fixed), and src/mprsurge/plotting/figures.py line 854, in `_journal_tail`, the Provenance text `Journal export of {fig_id} (draft = {str(prov['draft']).lower()}, untagged), commit ...` (the word untagged is fixed; the draft value there is read from the record). IS THERE A CIRCULAR TAG? In the code, no: tag_build checks only that the tree is clean; it does not require that a tag exists, does not read git.tags, and creates no tag; the plan's own workflow builds the figure and then tags it (plan lines 1257 and 1258: `python scripts\fig_F3.py` and then `git tag -a fig-F3-v1 -m ...`). So the flag can be made true without a tag: a release build is a build called with the tag option from a clean tree, the tags are placed after it (step 20). What stays UNVERIFIED: (a) that this is what the plan's L1284 ("Every provenance file names the release commit and none is marked DRAFT"; the plan defines neither "release commit" nor "provenance file") means; (b) the proposed reading that the release commit is the clean build commit R and that release-v1.0 and the fig-<ID>-v2 tags are placed on R plus documents-only commits (step 20 shows this with `git diff --stat R..<tag target>`); (c) that the 11 draft records (draft = true, commit 4e68752) are outside "every provenance file" (option B of the notes, as ruled; the drafts are audit copies). The record will say draft false, git.dirty false and git.tags [] (no tag exists at build time); the supplement says so in words that are true at that moment (see below). The STOP condition of D3 (a circular tag that cannot be avoided) therefore does not arise; the plan's L1284 wording is quoted word for word: "Every provenance file names the release commit and none is marked DRAFT." CHANGE PLAN (smallest; nothing else about what is drawn, written or hashed changes): (C-1) scripts/fig_journal.py: add `ap.add_argument("--tag", "--release", dest="tag", action="store_true", help="release build: the clean-tree check runs first (scripts/check_clean_tree.py) and a dirty tree stops the build before anything is written; provenance draft = false; no tag is created")`; if a.tag, run `subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(root / "scripts" / "check_clean_tree.py")])` before the first figure and return its code if it is not 0 (exactly the pattern of fig_F3.py); pass `tag_build=a.tag` in the make_<ID> call; module docstring: the build is an untagged DRAFT unless the option is given. Default behaviour (no option) is unchanged: draft = true, no clean-tree check. (C-2) src/mprsurge/plotting/journal.py: add `build_kind(draft: bool) -> str` returning "untagged" if draft else "release build, tags placed after the build"; `write_supplement(..., draft: bool = True)` writes `(journal export; draft = {str(draft).lower()})` in its first line; the default True gives the old first line byte for byte. (C-3) src/mprsurge/plotting/figures.py `_journal_tail`: the Provenance text uses `{J.build_kind(prov['draft'])}` in place of the fixed word untagged, and `J.write_supplement(..., draft=prov['draft'])`. For a draft build both texts are byte-identical to before. NEW WORDING for a release build (true at build time because no tag exists and the tree is clean): first line `# <ID> supplement sheet (journal export; draft = false)`; Provenance text `Journal export of <ID> (draft = false, release build, tags placed after the build), commit <R>, git dirty = false. Provenance file: ...` (the rest of the sentence unchanged). figprov.py is NOT changed. TESTS (new file tests/test_ms15a_draft_flag.py; logged here before the file is written; the file is committed before it is run): (1) test_journal_script_default_is_a_draft_build_without_a_tree_check (make_<ID> receives tag_build False, no check_clean_tree call); (2) test_journal_script_release_checks_the_tree_first_and_passes_tag_build (the check runs before the first make call; tag_build True; both option spellings --tag and --release); (3) test_journal_script_release_on_a_dirty_tree_builds_nothing (exit code of the check returned, no make call, no manifest); (4) test_provenance_draft_is_false_only_for_a_clean_tagged_build (the four combinations of dirty and tag_build through figprov.write_figure_provenance with dirty_lines monkeypatched; dirty with tag_build raises DirtyTreeError and writes nothing); (5) test_supplement_first_line_follows_the_flag (draft False, True and the default); (6) test_build_kind_wording (both words); (7) test_journal_tail_has_no_fixed_draft_or_untagged_text (inspect.getsource of figures._journal_tail and journal.write_supplement: no fixed "untagged" and no fixed "draft = true"). Tolerances: all comparisons exact (strings, booleans, exit codes). THE BUILD COMMIT R (D5; recorded here before the build): the prompt asks that R be the one clean commit the figures are built from, HEAD = R, and that R be recorded in the log before the build. A log entry is itself a commit, so R cannot be the code commit and also hold its own hash. Defined here: C = the commit that adds scripts/fig_journal.py, journal.py and figures.py changes (its hash is recorded in the entry that follows); R = HEAD at the moment of the build = the commit that adds the next decision-log entry ("build commit entry"), which differs from C in docs/decision_log.md only (shown with `git diff --stat C..R` in that entry). The provenance records name R (git.commit = HEAD at build). If the user wants R = C literally, the log entry would have to be made after the build; that cannot hold with "record R in the log before building" and a clean tree, so this definition is used and reported (UNVERIFIED reading of the prompt). The build is run once: `.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\fig_journal.py --release F1 F2 F3 F4a F4b F5 F5c F6 FS1 FS2 FS3 FS4 FS5`, from R, tree clean.
